added.title: Specialist Solutions Architect, Crypto & Stablecoins
added.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSA) are domain experts aligned to specific Stripe solutions and customer buying centers. We have in-depth knowledge of specific solution offerings and a deep understanding of customer challenges. We align with specialist product sellers on deals, advise the broader pre-sales team on complex opportunities, support pipeline development and revenue attainment, serve as an advisor on go-to-market sales plays, and provide critical insights to our product and engineering teams.

What You'll Do

You will collaborate closely with sales and pre-sales teams to drive pipeline and revenue targets, while also educating the product and engineering teams on market trends and strongly influencing the product roadmap. You will develop deep relationships with senior customer business leaders and grow Stripe's solution offerings with new and existing customers. As a subject matter expert, you will scale the broader organization by creating reusable assets and coaching others on complex, high-value opportunities.

As a Specialist Solutions Architect for Crypto and Stablecoins, you will lead in-depth product discussions with Stripe's top users and prospects and execute against our go-to-market strategy for Stripe's crypto and stablecoin products, including Bridge and Privy. You will serve as a trusted advisor for business and technical stakeholders—CTOs, CFOs, Heads of Digital Assets, and Treasury teams—helping them understand how stablecoin infrastructure can power faster, cheaper, and more programmable money movement globally.

Responsibilities

Act as a subject matter expert on Stripe's crypto and stablecoin products—including Bridge and Privy—to accelerate opportunities globally
Demonstrate a deep understanding of money movement use cases and how Stripe's crypto and stablecoin products address customer needs
Understand the regulatory landscape and compliance requirements for crypto and stablecoin implementations across jurisdictions (MiCA, US regulatory landscape, and beyond)
Define, share, and learn best practices and reusable assets with the broader GTM organization to enhance the quality and efficiency of the team
Create reference architectures to uplevel the team and refine reference solutions based on product enhancements and customer feedback
Partner closely with the crypto product sales team on Stripe's largest crypto opportunities, leading solution strategy and owning key customer relationships
Partner closely with the product teams to get early exposure to new products and features
Serve as a "Voice of the Customer" internally to drive product and feature request prioritization
Identify and summarize trends in the stablecoin and digital asset ecosystem, and provide actionable insights to product stakeholders and sales
Act as an escalation point to drive complex technical issues to resolution with Stripe's engineering team
Stay current on competitive analysis and market differentiation in the digital asset space
Support marketing events including executive briefings, conferences, and trade shows focused on crypto and blockchain technology

Who You Are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of technical sales or solutions engineering experience, ideally within fintech, crypto, or blockchain companies.
Deep experience designing or implementing solutions in at least one of two domains: fiat payments and money movement, such as payment processing, cross-border payments, remittances, or banking-as-a-service; or blockchain and digital assets, such as blockchain platforms, wallets, custody, or digital asset applications.
Experience working with APIs and integrating financial or blockchain infrastructure into customers’ existing systems.
Ability and willingness to build expertise in the complementary domain. Prior experience in both fiat and crypto money movement is not required.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, comfortable explaining complex financial and technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners.
Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of hands-on experience with crypto and stablecoin financial services, particularly payments, cross-border transfers, settlement, or fiat-to-crypto on- and off-ramps.
Strong knowledge of regulatory frameworks across the Americas governing digital assets, cross-border payments, and international money movement, particularly the US regulatory landscape.
Experience designing and deploying complex applications that integrate blockchain infrastructure with traditional financial and payment systems.
Experience enabling and scaling a GTM team in the crypto or fintech space.
Background in treasury management, corporate finance, or digital asset custody solutions.
Experience establishing a new regional capability, launching a new solution in-market, or building repeatable customer engagement practices in an early-stage environment.

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $203,400 - $305,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

added.title: Staff Data Scientist, Product Marketing
added.description:
About The Role

Chime is looking for a Staff Data Scientist to establish the analytical direction for Product Marketing (PMM). As PMM’s dedicated analytics partner, you will help leaders forecast card demand, understand how members discover and activate Chime products, and connect member research with behavioral evidence to guide strategy and investment.

Your work will span three priorities. You will evolve card demand planning into a rigorous, repeatable forecasting process. You will build on existing research and analytical prototypes to establish reliable measurement of product activation and the member lifecycle, from account opening and first direct deposit through adoption, engagement, and retention. You will also partner with Research to translate qualitative findings into testable hypotheses and assess how broadly those findings apply across the member population.

As a Staff individual contributor, you will define ambiguous problems, set analytical standards, and deliver practical solutions. You will establish a prioritized roadmap with PMM leadership and partner with Product, Growth Analytics, Research, Card Operations, Finance, Data Engineering, and Enterprise Data & Metrics to turn analytical work into trusted data products and business decisions.

In this role, you can expect to

Build reliable card demand forecasting

Own the methodology for card demand forecasting, translating business planning needs into appropriate forecast horizons, granularity, refresh schedules, and performance measures.
Develop and evaluate time-series and driver-based models incorporating member growth, product launches, marketing activity, seasonality, replacement demand, and other relevant inputs.
Establish historical backtesting, benchmark comparisons, forecast bias and error monitoring, and uncertainty estimates. Investigate misses and continuously improve performance.
Partner with PMM, Card Operations, and Finance to translate forecasts into planning scenarios and assess implications for inventory, supplier lead times, cost, and service risk.
Build reproducible forecasting workflows with documented assumptions, stakeholder inputs, monitoring, and clear ownership.

Establish product activation and member lifecycle measurement

Define measurement frameworks for product discovery, activation, adoption, and sustained engagement across the member lifecycle, accounting for cohort, tenure, eligibility, and member segment.
Build on existing activation research and analytical prototypes to establish production-ready measurement, including cohort analyses anchored to milestones such as first qualifying direct deposit.
Evaluate proposed operating metrics, including Activated Member Rate, assessing product selection, thresholds, observation windows, sensitivity, and relationships with downstream engagement and retention.
Balance timely operational signals with cohort maturity and analytical validity. Distinguish predictive relationships from causal evidence and identify where further validation is needed.
Identify friction and drop-off across onboarding and cross-product journeys, size opportunities, and recommend actions to improve activation and sustained use.
Partner with Enterprise Data & Metrics and source-data owners to develop tested dbt models, historical backfills, governed metric definitions, and reliable Hex reporting.
Establish metric governance, versioning, and historical comparability as products, eligibility rules, and definitions evolve.
Create recurring monitoring and business-review mechanisms that help PMM understand performance and distinguish changes in member behavior from the incremental impact of its initiatives.

Connect member research with quantitative evidence

Partner with User Research and PMM to translate qualitative findings about member needs, motivations, and barriers into testable hypotheses.
Use behavioral data, segmentation, funnel analysis, and statistical methods to assess the prevalence of research findings and how they differ across member groups.
Combine qualitative and quantitative evidence to guide positioning, messaging, onboarding, and product adoption strategies.
Design, power, and interpret experiments to evaluate these strategies, coordinating analytical ownership with Product and Growth Analytics.
Apply appropriate causal inference methods when randomization is not feasible, clearly communicating assumptions, uncertainty, and limitations.
Identify where behavioral evidence and research findings diverge, and recommend follow-up analysis or research to resolve the gaps.

Lead analytical strategy and influence decisions

Establish PMM’s analytics roadmap, balancing urgent forecasting needs with foundational measurement and longer-term strategic questions.
Set standards for forecasting, experimentation, metric validation, and interpretation within your scope.
Influence VP-level and executive decisions through clear recommendations, scenario analysis, and compelling written and verbal communication.
Resolve conflicting assumptions, definitions, and priorities across PMM, Product, Growth, Finance, and other partners.
Use AI tools to accelerate analysis, coding, and research synthesis while validating outputs and maintaining reproducibility.
Raise the analytical bar through methodological guidance, peer review, and reusable tools and approaches.

To thrive in this role, you have

A bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Operations Research, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Extensive experience in analytics or data science, with a track record of independently setting analytical direction, solving ambiguous problems, and influencing decisions across multiple teams.
Hands-on experience building and operating demand forecasts used in business planning. You can explain how you selected methods, evaluated performance, quantified uncertainty, investigated errors, and incorporated stakeholder inputs.

Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSA) are domain experts aligned to specific Stripe solutions and customer buying centers. We have in-depth knowledge of specific solution offerings and a deep understanding of customer challenges. We align with specialist product sellers on deals, advise the broader pre-sales team on complex opportunities, support pipeline development and revenue attainment, serve as an advisor on go-to-market sales plays, and provide critical insights to our product and engineering teams.

What You'll Do

You will collaborate closely with sales and pre-sales teams to drive pipeline and revenue targets, while also educating the product and engineering teams on market trends and strongly influencing the product roadmap. You will develop deep relationships with senior customer business leaders and grow Stripe's solution offerings with new and existing customers. As a subject matter expert, you will scale the broader organization by creating reusable assets and coaching others on complex, high-value opportunities.

Responsibilities

Act as a subject matter expert on Stripe's Data products (data pipelines/export, revenue and reconciliation reporting, and analytics tooling) to accelerate opportunities
Demonstrate a deep understanding of how businesses warehouse and model payments and revenue data — data pipelines into Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks; ETL/ELT patterns; and how that data feeds financial reporting, reconciliation, and BI
Conduct deep discovery of customers' existing data architecture, warehouse, and reporting stack to architect solutions that align Stripe's Data capabilities with their analytics and finance requirements
Advise customers on how to design for complexity: multi-entity and multi-currency reporting, custom data models, integration with existing BI tools (Looker, Tableau, Sigma, Metabase) and ERP/GL systems, and data freshness/latency requirements
Create and share best practices and reusable assets such as reference architectures to enhance the quality and efficiency of the broader sales and pre-sales organizations
Partner closely with the Data product sales team and actively drive opportunities for Stripe's largest customers, leading solution strategy and owning key customer relationships
Serve as a "Voice of the Customer" to drive product and feature request prioritization
Identify product, industry, implementation, and competitive trends, and provide actionable insights to product stakeholders and sales to influence Stripe's Data product roadmap
Act as an escalation point to drive complex technical issues to resolution with Stripe's engineering team
Represent the technical health of the business on quarterly sales forecast calls and highlight deal blockers with proposed solutions
Support marketing events including executive briefings, conferences, user groups, and trade shows

Who You Are

You're capable of engaging in both business-level and technical conversations at multiple levels of a customer organization, including finance, data, and engineering leadership. You enjoy working on products that require deep technical understanding combined with business context, and you're as comfortable in a warehouse schema as you are in a revenue conversation with a CFO. You're excited to become an expert and to share that knowledge broadly.

If you meet the minimum requirements below, we encourage you to apply — the preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of experience in a technical sales, pre-sales, or solutions architecture role, with a focus on data platforms, analytics, or financial reporting
3+ years of hands-on experience with data warehousing and pipeline architecture (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks) and ETL/ELT tooling
Strong understanding of how payments and revenue data maps to financial reporting and reconciliation workflows
Experience working with or implementing BI/analytics platforms (Looker, Tableau, Sigma, Metabase, or similar)
Strong knowledge of software engineering and API integration patterns, including how data pipelines are built and maintained
Exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, comfortable explaining complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners
Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience integrating Stripe or other RESTful APIs into data pipelines or web applications
Familiarity with complex reporting scenarios: multi-entity consolidation, revenue recognition data models, or usage-based billing data
Experience with SQL at an advanced level and comfort working directly in a customer's data warehouse during discovery
Experience as a subject matter expert in financial services, fintech, or a data/analytics vertical
Pre-sales experience with Enterprise customers

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $239,900 - $359,900. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Founding Engineer — AI/ML · Robotics Data

Nua · San Francisco, CA · On-site · Full-time
$120,000 – $240,000 base + equity

About Nua

Robotics and AI companies generate enormous volumes of raw sensor, video and trajectory data, and almost none of it arrives in a form a model can learn from. Nua labels, annotates and formats that data so robotics builders and data providers can spend their time training models instead of wrangling inputs.

We are a three-person, founder-led team in San Francisco, five months in, already working with robotics companies and data providers, and funded to make this hire now.

The Role

You will be Nua’s first engineer outside the founding team. You will work directly with the founders on whatever moves the company furthest that week: improving the models behind our pipeline one day, shipping the platform customers use the next. There is no narrow lane and no one to hand things off to. The engineer who takes this role will shape how Nua builds for years.

What you will do

Improve the models behind Nua’s labeling and annotation pipeline: data quality, training, evaluation, and the loop between them
Build and extend the platform customers rely on: ingestion, formatting, tooling and APIs
Own problems end to end, from a customer’s raw data drop to a training-ready output
Establish the engineering practices Nua will hire against next: how code is reviewed, tested, shipped and measured
Move between model work and product work as priorities shift, often within the same week

What you bring

Hands-on machine learning or AI engineering: you have trained, fine-tuned, evaluated or deployed models in real systems
Strong software fundamentals; you ship production code outside the model as readily as inside it
Comfort with breadth and ambiguity; you would rather carry five problems at once than specialize early
Based in San Francisco, or willing to relocate; the team works together in person
A clear-eyed view of early-stage pace: this is not a 9-to-5, and the hours reflect that

There is no years-of-experience threshold. We weigh what you have built and what you can build here.

Nice to have

Robotics exposure: perception, sensor data, simulation, policy learning, or data pipelines for robot learning
Experience with data labeling, annotation or dataset tooling
Prior founding-engineer or seed-stage startup experience

Why Nua

Founding-engineer scope with customers already in place, so the work ships instead of waiting on product-market fit
A direct line to the founders on every technical and product decision
A seat at the data layer of the robotics stack, the part every model builder depends on and few have solved well
Compensation that scales with experience, plus founding-team equity

Compensation and location

Base salary of $120,000 to $240,000, set by the depth and relevance of your experience. Equity is part of the package and is discussed during the process. The role is on-site in San Francisco; candidates outside the Bay Area are welcome if able to relocate.

Nua is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

This job is part of LinkedIn’s Full-Service Hiring beta program. Eligibility is limited to candidates located in and performing services in the United States, excluding those based in Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, South Carolina, or West Virginia.

If you don’t hear from us in that time, we encourage you to explore other opportunities with our team in the future, and we wish you the very best in your job search.

ECG is a national consulting firm that is redefining healthcare together with its clients. We provide a broad range of strategic, financial, operational, and technology-enabled consulting services to the full continuum of care, including hospitals, health systems, medical groups, academic medical centers, children’s hospitals, cancer centers, ambulatory surgery centers, investors, and payers/health plans.

Our work focuses on creating practical, tailored solutions that help clients maximize resources and achieve sustainable results. We value collaboration, integrity, and innovation, and are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment.

Job Details

Join Our Analytics Hub

Our growing Analytics Hub works with our consulting teams to deliver new insights, streamlined analysis, and world-class intelligence to the healthcare organizations we serve as clients. Combined with our consulting teams, you will be helping physician and executive leadership make informed decisions that can alter the course of their enterprises in areas such as physician alignment, mergers and acquisitions, service line planning, provider compensation, financial performance, transforming care models, patient access, managed care portfolio optimization, digital health expansion, and more. Our detailed plans incorporate qualitative findings with data-driven strategic, operational, and financial considerations that enable organizations to pursue realistic change. Position themselves for value-based care delivery.
Align hospitals and physician organizations.
Strengthen financial performance.
Enhance clinical programs.
Develop strategic partnerships and/or mergers.

Your Opportunity with ECG: Senior Healthcare AI Engineer

As a senior healthcare AI engineer, you will help drive the firm's AI strategy by designing, developing, and deploying intelligent solutions that enhance client delivery, accelerate internal operations, and create new service offerings. Working closely with consultants, healthcare subject matter experts, data engineers, and business leaders, you will transform complex healthcare and business challenges into scalable AI-powered applications.

In addition, you will partner with internal teams including IT, learning and development, business development, and analytics engineering to establish AI best practices, evaluate emerging technologies, and build secure, governed, and scalable AI capabilities across the organization. Here, no two days or projects are alike, which means you’ll have a lot to learn and plenty of support to help you succeed.

We are seeking an innovative and technically skilled senior healthcare AI engineer to design, develop, and deploy AI solutions that improve healthcare operations, clinical decision-making, and business performance. This individual will work at the intersection of healthcare, data science, software engineering, and generative AI, developing scalable solutions that utilize healthcare data to create actionable insights and automate complex workflows.

Design and develop production-grade generative AI, ML, and agentic AI solutions for healthcare and business applications.
Collaborate with IT and Hub members to deploy solutions.
Build retrieval-augmented generation systems, intelligent assistants, AI agents, and workflow automation solutions using enterprise and healthcare data.

Design scalable architectures that support customer-facing AI applications, agentic workflows, and intelligent automation solutions.
Build and maintain CI/CD processes, monitoring capabilities, and deployment pipelines for AI applications.

Collaborate with IT, cybersecurity, and governance teams to ensure secure deployment and compliance with firm requirements.

Ensure AI systems comply with HIPAA, security, privacy, and regulatory requirements (e.g., SOC2, HITRUST), where applicable.
Contribute to AI governance practices around model monitoring, fairness, transparency, explainability, and risk mitigation.
Collaborate with cybersecurity and data governance teams to ensure secure deployment of AI solutions.

Partner with division leaders, healthcare consultants, clinicians, and operational stakeholders to identify AI opportunities.
Translate business requirements into technical AI solutions.
Present findings, recommendations, and system capabilities to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Stay current with emerging AI technologies, healthcare innovation, and industry best practices.

Strong knowledge of and passion for the healthcare industry
Bachelor’s degree in either computer science, computer engineering, mathematics, statistics, health information management, or a related degree that relies heavily on critical thinking, logic, and math
A master's degree is a plus

5+ years of professional experience working in data engineering or data science
Healthcare or consulting experience is preferred

2+ years of recent experience developing production AI, ML, or advanced analytics solutions
Strong proficiency in:

Experience with agentic AI frameworks and LLM evaluation frameworks

Experience working with healthcare data, healthcare technology, healthcare consulting, health systems, payer organizations, or digital health companies
Experience deploying agents from Azure AI Foundry and/or Microsoft Copilot Studio
Experience using the Microsoft Fabric platform

Other locations: Boston

Full time/exempt

To reward our driven, innovative, and passionate employees, we’ve built a company culture that’s centered on performance. We offer an attractive compensation package, challenging work, and an entrepreneurial environment where you can take ownership of your career—and get out as much as you put in.

Raytheon’s Data, Analytics and AI organization is seeking a Senior Agentic AI Engineer
to design, develop, and deploy enterprise-scale AI agents and intelligent automation solutions that transform how work gets done. In this role, you will develop advanced agentic AI systems capable of reasoning, planning, decision-making, and autonomous execution across complex business processes.

As a Senior Agentic AI Engineer, you will combine expertise in agent orchestration, generative AI, large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), machine learning, and enterprise systems integration to deliver scalable, production-ready AI solutions. From strategy and architecture through deployment and optimization, you will help shape the next generation of AI-powered business capabilities.

Generative AI & LLM Engineering: Develop LLM-powered applications, optimize model selection, prompt engineering, context management, and inference performance.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) & Knowledge Integration: Design and implement RAG solutions, including data ingestion, embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, and knowledge retrieval.
AI/ML Model Development: Apply machine learning, classification, predictive analytics, and other AI techniques to solve complex business problems and enhance agent capabilities.
Enterprise Systems Integration: Build APIs, data pipelines, and integrations connecting AI agents with enterprise applications, databases, and business workflows.
Production Deployment & Optimization: Implement testing, evaluation, CI/CD, monitoring, security guardrails, and performance optimization to ensure scalable, reliable production solutions.
Technical Leadership & Innovation: Establish reusable AI components, and reference architecture while evaluating emerging AI technologies and mentoring development teams.

,

. The primary responsibility of this role is to design, build, and operationalize an enterprise-grade ML platform on AWS SageMaker AI
or Unified Studio.

Stay current with evolving AI/ML platform technologies and engineering best practices.

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field that provides a strong foundation in software engineering, cloud platforms, or machine learning.
4+ years of DevOps or Software Engineering experience in cloud infrastructure or ML platform operations.
2+ years of hands-on AWS experience, including Amazon SageMaker Studio, Pipelines, Model Registry, Endpoints, and Feature Store.
2+ years of experience building and operating production MLOps pipelines, including training, versioning, deployment, and rollback strategies.
Proficiency with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, CDK, or CloudFormation to build repeatable, and scalable environments.
Working understanding of IAM design for ML, including execution roles, service roles, and cross-account access management.
Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work independently while partnering effectively across teams.

Added bonus if you have

Advanced knowledge of SageMaker AI, including domain provisioning, custom blueprints, and project standardization.
An AWS Machine Learning Specialty certification that demonstrates deeper technical expertise.

Job Summary

The Principal AI Engineer provides technical leadership in the design, development, training, orchestration, and operationalization of enterprise AI systems. This role defines strategy and technical standards across traditional AI/ML models, large language models, model training and fine-tuning, data and retrieval systems, and agentic AI architectures. The Principal AI Engineer remains deeply hands-on while partnering across product and platform teams to build scalable, reliable, secure, and high-quality AI capabilities.

Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities

Define and own technical strategy across enterprise AI systems, spanning traditional AI/ML models, large language models, model training and fine-tuning, retrieval, orchestration, and agentic AI.
Design, train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize traditional AI/ML models and large language models using parameter-efficient techniques (e.g., QLoRA, LoRA, PEFT) and full fine-tuning where warranted.
Design orchestration and abstraction layers that connect LLMs to enterprise tools, data, APIs, and specialized sub-agents while decoupling product teams from underlying models and providers.
Design, build, and operate MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and establish standards for how AI tools and capabilities are defined, exposed, versioned, and consumed.
Design and optimize retrieval (RAG) systems, including chunking strategies, embedding models, vector stores, hybrid/keyword search, re-ranking, and context assembly.
Design and optimize data pipelines for ingestion, cleaning, labeling, feature engineering, storage, versioning, and reuse of training, validation, and test datasets.
Build reproducible AI/ML pipelines and establish standards for experiment tracking, dataset management, model versioning, checkpoints, metrics, and evaluation.

Build routing, context-window management, memory, observability, and tracing strategies for multi-step and agentic AI workflows.
Establish practices for AI data governance, lineage, quality, licensing/consent, PII handling, safety, guardrails, authentication, and access control.
Partner with product and platform teams to operationalize AI capabilities, onboard tools and agents, and transition trained and fine-tuned models into production.
Mentor engineers, establish technical standards and best practices, and raise AI engineering maturity across teams.

12 or more years of experience in AI/ML engineering, applied ML, or data engineering, with significant hands-on model training and fine-tuning
Strong hands-on experience designing, training, fine-tuning, and deploying traditional AI/ML models and large language models in production environments.
Deep experience with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (QLoRA, LoRA, PEFT), quantization, model evaluation, and the tradeoffs between fine-tuning approaches.
Deep hands-on experience with LLM orchestration, agentic AI patterns, MCP servers, tool/function calling, and frameworks such as LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or equivalents.
Deep experience with retrieval/RAG architectures, including chunking strategies, embeddings, vector databases, hybrid search, re-ranking, and context assembly.

Experience building and operating scalable data and AI pipelines and platforms using technologies such as Spark, Ray, dbt, or equivalents.

added.description:
About Leon Capital Group

Leon Capital Group is a multi-billion-dollar holding company with operating businesses across healthcare, real estate, and financial services. Within the Financial Services Group (FSG), we are building an AI-native operating model from the ground up: a dedicated, full-lifecycle innovation function that identifies, designs, builds, delivers, and implements AI products across our portfolio companies.

About the Role

This is two halves of one job: The Data Platform & Machine Learning Engineer
will own the data platform every FSG and healthcare AI product depends on, and you build the first machine learning models on top of it. The two are inseparable, because the models are only as good as the proprietary, provenance-tracked data beneath them, and that data is yours to design, capture, and own. Not a pipeline specialist, not a modeling specialist, but the engineer who does both, as a member of a small data platform team, on foundations that range from ones you stand up yourself to established platforms you extend and modernize.

The role has a deliberate arc. The first few months lean heavily toward data engineering: the canonical model and warehouse, ingestion that forces messy external data into our schema, and judgment capture that turns every human decision into labeled training data. As that corpus matures, the center of gravity shifts toward building the first risk and recommendation models on it. You work across portfolio companies in both FSG and healthcare, standing up or extending each one's data layer and models and reusing the same patterns and discipline rather than reinventing the approach each time. We want someone energized by both halves, not someone tolerating the foundation to reach the models, or the reverse.

You will work across both ends of the maturity curve. Some portfolio companies run established platforms (cloud warehouses, dbt, orchestration, BI) that need extending, hardening, and integrating; others, including businesses we acquire, run on spreadsheets, vendor portals, and flat-file feeds with no platform at all. You need to be productive in both: respecting what already works in a mature stack, and building from zero where nothing exists.

You will also be expected to use AI as part of how you work, not only what you build. A small team covering two sectors and many portfolio companies only scales if everyone already uses AI tools every day to write and review code, draft pipelines and tests, profile data, and explore modeling approaches. The bar is judgment: you verify what AI produces, own everything you ship, and know when not to use it. Unreviewed output and blind trust in a model are not acceptable here, and critical thinking matters more to us than any tool.

Key Responsibilities

Co-design and own key components of the canonical data model and warehouse, built to remain ours regardless of which vendors we buy.
Build the data platform and models as reusable patterns, standing up each portfolio company's own instance rather than a bespoke build each time.
Work across mature and immature stacks: extend and integrate with established platforms where they exist, and stand up lightweight, production-ready foundations from zero where they do not.
Migrate and modernize legacy pipelines and data stores onto the shared platform without disrupting the reporting and operations that depend on them.
Build ingestion pipelines that pull from hostile, heterogeneous sources into our schema with full provenance, including vendor servicing output, flat-file and SFTP partner feeds with no API, and public registry data.
Stand up judgment capture from the first transaction: structure every decision and correction as labeled training data, the raw material that human-in-the-loop workflows and future models both depend on.
Lay the groundwork for risk and recommendation models: feature engineering, training-set construction, model evaluation, and calibration.
Build validation, monitoring, and lineage so data-quality issues are caught before they reach models or decisions.
Enforce the data-ownership bar in every buy decision: vendor output must land in our canonical structure, in our schema, and remain portable on exit.
Partner closely with AI Engineers, providing the models, data, and serving interfaces their decision surfaces and the production AI agents already live in the portfolio are built on.

Qualifications

Required:

5+ years building data systems end to end, including required experience at a startup or in a 0-to-1 build environment, as an early or founding data hire who took a data function from nothing to production rather than owning one stage of a large team.
Hands-on experience with both mature and immature data stacks: you have worked inside an established modern data platform (e.g., a cloud warehouse or lakehouse, dbt, Airflow or Dagster, CI/CD for data) and you have built where there was no platform at all. You know when to adopt the existing pattern and when to build from scratch.
AI-augmented daily practice.
You already use AI to accelerate your engineering work and can show how: what you delegate, how you verify it, and where it got something wrong and you caught it. You treat AI output as a draft to be challenged, not an answer to be trusted. Critical thinking comes first; tool fluency comes second.
Strong data engineering fundamentals: schema design, ETL and ELT pipeline architecture, and production experience with PostgreSQL.
Comfort owning data infrastructure in a major cloud environment (we use a mix across Azure and AWS); you can stand up and run the warehouse and pipelines without a dedicated platform team.
Comfort building under regulatory and fiduciary constraints, and handling sensitive, regulated data (PHI under HIPAA, and financial and policyholder data) with the secure practices it requires.
Applied machine learning and statistical modeling depth: feature work, model evaluation, calibration, and the judgment to reason about model risk. You orchestrate and apply models; you do not need to publish research.
Working fluency with LLM orchestration and agentic workflows (e.g. LangGraph) on production model platforms (e.g. Anthropic Claude, AWS Bedrock), retrieval-augmented generation, and disciplined prompt and evaluation practices.
Excellent judgment under ambiguity and the ability to prioritize across multiple portfolio companies without close oversight.

Note to Search Firms and Agencies:

Leon Capital Group does not accept unsolicited submissions from search firms or employment agencies. Any resume submitted to any employee of Leon Capital Group without a valid written search agreement in place will be deemed the sole property of Leon Capital Group, and no fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired.

Vectra® is the leader in AI-driven threat detection and response for hybrid and multi-cloud enterprises.

The Vectra AI Platform delivers integrated signal across public cloud, SaaS, identity, and data center networks in a single platform. Powered by patented Attack Signal Intelligence, it empowers security teams to rapidly prioritize, investigate and respond to the most advanced cyber-attacks. With 35 patents in AI-driven threat detection and the most vendor references in MITRE D3FEND, organizations worldwide rely on the Vectra AI to move at the speed and scale of hybrid attackers. For more information, visit www.vectra.ai.

Vectra AI delivers a new class of advanced threat defense that delivers real-time detection and response for cloud and network intrusions. Vectra technology picks up where perimeter security leaves off by providing deep, continuous analysis of both on-premises network traffic and cloud-computing activity to automatically detect all phases of a cyberattack.

Vectra applies a variety of data analysis, modeling, and machine learning techniques to detect malicious and anomalous behavior in real-time streams of traffic and log metadata. Detected events are correlated and prioritized to show an attack in context, enabling faster response and remediation. Vectra's machine learning generalizes to new approaches and tools, keeping customers protected even as attack techniques evolve.

Position Overview

Be on the leading edge of applying machine learning and data modeling to the world of advanced cyber security. As part of the Data Science team you will directly impact the product by solving complex problems, modeling data relating to network and cloud environments, and developing production software. You will work with diverse datasets and problems across multiple areas, including detecting cyber-attacks in real-time, building advanced prioritization systems for detections, and leveraging AI at the user interface. You will work in direct collaboration with Security Researchers, who are experts in cyber security attack techniques.

Responsibilities

Be a leader in the team by being a technical resource or mentor for Data Scientists on areas of machine learning, statistics, and software engineering.
Leverage large datasets to develop machine learning and statistical models that can differentiate between normal and attack behaviors.
Drive exploratory and feature projects to bring machine learning and AI approaches to areas such as user-interfaces and detection prioritization.
Own the prototyping, development, and testing of complex algorithms that implement these models and provide customers with real-time visibility.
Present key findings to business leaders from exploratory and feature project work.
Collaborate with Security Research, Data Engineering, and Software Engineering teammates.

3-4 years professional experience in Data Science and/or Machine Learning Engineering
MS/PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics or related discipline
Hands-on experience with machine learning and statistical techniques

added.description:
About TTS-US:

Founded in 2011, Toyota Tsusho Systems US, Inc. (TTS-US) is a Toyota group company, that develops IT solutions wherever global businesses operate. Transforming into a technology and mobility company, TTS-US with it's 8 TTS affiliates worldwide is establishing a secure and resilient Toyota global value chain. The creative capacity to forge such limitless business opportunities is one of the strengths of Toyota Tsusho Systems.

Summary:

The Product Cybersecurity Group is building an AI harness that brings Generative and agentic AI capabilities to Product Cybersecurity engineering. The Principal AI Security Software Engineer works hands-on with the team, building the prompts, agents, tools, connectors, and workflows that make AI perform real Product Cybersecurity work across PCG workflows and customer environments.

This is a hands-on engineering role. The Principal AI Security Software Engineer spends most of their time writing, testing, and shipping code alongside the team, rather than producing architecture documents for others to implement. This role does not train foundation models. Instead, the engineer takes existing models and makes them perform useful, reliable, measurable work by building the full path from prototype to production, including the data access, orchestration, evaluation, and observability that make AI features trustworthy enough for use in security-sensitive environments.

The Principal AI Security Software Engineer brings a software developer's mindset to AI, including version control, code review, testing, debugging, and maintainable design. The engineer works as part of the team, partnering with engineers, turning security tasks into working AI-assisted workflows, and helping team members learn to build and extend those workflows themselves.

Essential Functions:

Build (the majority of the role)
Write and ship the components that make AI do the work — prompts, agents, skills, tools, MCP servers, connectors, scripts, and orchestration logic — assembled into end-to-end LLM applications such as retrieval pipelines, agent workflows, and structured-output workflows
Turn the team's manual security tasks into working AI-assisted workflows, such as engineering analysis, knowledge retrieval, documentation, requirements analysis, code/design review, test generation, and security-assessment support
Securely connect the harness to approved customer documentation, knowledge sources, repositories, APIs, identity systems, and downstream tools so AI operates with relevant context
Build a reusable library of components so each new use case is faster to deliver than the last
Shape the technical approach
Make and document practical design decisions for the harness — model integration, context management, tool integration — so the team can build on them
Contribute design and code reviews that keep components maintainable, secure, and reusable
Recommend when to build, reuse, or stop an approach based on evidence from working implementations
Measure
Build evaluations and quality gates for the workflows you ship — covering output quality, groundedness, hallucination rate, reliability, security, usefulness, latency, and cost — so releases rest on evidence rather than demo impressions
Analyze production transcripts and user feedback to drive iterative improvement
Operate
Version, test, deploy, monitor, and maintain prompts, context, and components with the same discipline as any other code
Design for reliability — provider or model fallback, graceful degradation, timeouts, and retries — and treat inference cost and latency as first-class constraints
Implement security practices — access controls, data handling, traceability, guardrails — aligned with internal and customer requirements, and release changes through existing change-management and security review processes
Work with the Team
Pair with team members and customer engineers to understand their work, identify the highest-value tasks for AI, and build solutions together
Help define what AI should and should not be used for, explaining technical constraints in terms non-specialists can act on
Teach by building: write clear examples, document how components work, and help engineers create and extend their own AI workflows

Competencies:

Advanced software engineering and application development expertise
Strong knowledge of Generative AI, agentic AI systems, prompt engineering, context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and LLM application development
Ability to evaluate, troubleshoot, and improve complex AI-enabled workflows using measurable performance criteria
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and non-technical audiences
Ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and mentor engineers through hands-on development and knowledge sharing
Demonstrated critical thinking, innovation, sound judgment, and the ability to solve complex technical problems in security-sensitive environments

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
8+ years of professional software development experience, with a track record of personally writing, shipping, and maintaining production software
Solid software engineering fundamentals: version control, code review, automated testing, debugging, and maintainable design
Hands-on experience building LLM-powered applications or AI-assisted workflows, including prompting and context engineering, retrieval (RAG), agent and tool-use frameworks, and evaluation; production experience strongly preferred
Practical experience with model APIs from at least one major provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or an open-weight equivalent)
Cloud experience (AWS, Azure, or GCP), containerization, and CI/CD
Experience designing secure systems: access controls, data handling, traceability, and guardrails for sensitive data
Ability to reason rigorously about non-deterministic systems and understand why a passing demo is not equivalent to a passing test
Strong written and verbal communication; able to explain tradeoffs to engineers and executives alike

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience building agentic AI systems: tool usage, workflow orchestration, multi-step autonomous workflows, and human-in-the-loop patterns
Experience with MCP, agent orchestration frameworks, and observability/tracing for LLM applications
Background in Product Cybersecurity, application security, or security-assessment workflows
Experience defining evaluation frameworks for AI output quality, reliability, and safety
Familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps practices for versioning, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining AI systems
Familiarity with AI governance and risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act) and secure handling of sensitive data in AI systems
Experience running technical workshops, pairing, or mentoring engineers new to AI

added.description:
Discover What’s Possible At BetMGM

Ready to make your career legendary? Join us as we bring the magic of Vegas to our players. The BetMGM team has over 1,400 talented members, revolutionizing sports betting and online gaming in the United States and Canada. We’re a brand with technology at our hearts and the most driven and focused talent in the business.

Benefits

As a valued team member, we’re committed to giving you the resources and support you need to thrive. Our benefits and perks include:

Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and Disability Insurance
401(k) with company match
Pre-tax spending accounts including health care FSA and commuter savings
Flexible paid time off
Professional development reimbursement and ongoing skills training opportunities
Employee resource groups
Swag, ticket giveaways, and more!

At BetMGM, we recognize that every individual plays a meaningful role in our success. That’s why we’re committed to building a respectful, inclusive workplace. It’s the strategy behind every win. By meeting people where they are, we create a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive and a workplace that reflects our values, our people, and our drive to win.

The Opportunity

About The Role

The Sr. MLOps Engineer treats ML systems as software systems and owns the path from a trained model to a production endpoint that meets its latency, cost, and reliability budgets — across both batch scoring (SageMaker Batch Transform, Snowflake Cortex / Snowpark ML, dbt-orchestrated scoring) and real-time inference (SageMaker real-time endpoints, Lambda + Bedrock, sub-second feature serving). The Sr. Engineer builds the platform that data scientists and ML engineers ship on: feature store with guaranteed online/offline parity, model registry, CI/CD for ML, drift and quality monitoring, champion/challenger and shadow deployment scaffolding. This requires a software-engineering-first mindset — distributed systems, observability, and on-call instincts are the foundation; ML literacy makes them effective for this role. GenAI integration experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Responsibilities

ML Production Platform
Stand up and operate BetMGM's ML platform on AWS (SageMaker Training, Model Registry, Pipelines, Endpoints, Batch Transform) and Snowflake (Snowpark ML, Cortex), with Terraform-managed infrastructure
Build self-service scaffolds that let data scientists ship a model end-to-end without a ticket queue — cookie-cutter project templates with CI, drift monitoring, alerting, IaC, and Snowflake connectivity pre-baked

Batch and Real-Time Inference
Design and operate batch scoring pipelines — SageMaker Batch Transform, dbt-orchestrated scoring against Snowflake, Snowpark ML — with explicit freshness and cost SLAs.
Design and operate real-time inference paths — SageMaker real-time endpoints, Lambda + Bedrock for GenAI, API Gateway — with stated latency budgets (typically sub-100ms) and graceful degradation under load.
Own the feature store (SageMaker Feature Store, Tecton, or Feast) with guaranteed online/offline parity — training-serving skew is treated as an incident, not a tradeoff.

CI/CD and Deployment Patterns
Build CI/CD for ML — model registry, automated retraining triggers, model versioning, lineage from feature → training run → deployed model → live prediction.
Implement champion/challenger, shadow deployments, and canary releases as platform primitives so individual model teams do not reinvent them per project.

Monitoring, Drift & Reliability
Stand up drift detection, data quality, and model performance monitoring (Evidently, Arize, or SageMaker Model Monitor — pick one and standardize) with paging that routes to humans who can fix it.
Own MLOps incident response — production model failures are SEV events with postmortems.

Cost and Performance
Right-size endpoints, batch caching, request batching, and autoscaling. State cost-per-prediction targets up front and meet them.

GenAI Integration (Plus, Not Required)
Integrate LLM APIs (Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI) into production paths — RAG pipelines, agent eval frameworks, prompt versioning, cost and latency observability.
Partner with the Helix team on AI personalization workloads as they ramp toward March Madness 2027.
undefined
AI in the Engineering Loop
Direct AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, dbt Copilot) as a force multiplier across infrastructure code, eval suites, and model-serving glue — designing work for agents to do, not just accepting their suggestions.

Collaboration
Partner with the data engineering team on shared standards (Terraform modules, CI/CD patterns, observability, lineage).
Work alongside data scientists and analytics partners to land the right interfaces between research and production — opinionated about the boundary.
Coordinate with Entain India and contractor ML partners as workloads consolidate onto the BetMGM-owned platform.

Qualifications
BS or MS in Computer Science, Math, Statistics, Machine Learning, or other STEM field — or equivalent practical experience. Practical experience wins ties; a PhD is neither required nor a tiebreakers
Must-Haves
5+ years shipping software in production — Python, Docker, Kubernetes or ECS, CI/CD, distributed systems debugging — including time on-call.
3+ years operating ML in production — you have owned a model in prod that served real traffic, with stated latency and cost budgets and a runbook you wrote.
AWS depth across the SageMaker surface (Training, Endpoints, Batch Transform, Model Registry, Pipelines) plus the supporting cast (IAM, Lambda, ECS, S3, Secrets Manager, VPC).
Snowflake fluency — Snowpark ML, Cortex, dbt-orchestrated batch scoring, RBAC for ML workloads.
IaC for ML — Terraform + SageMaker Pipelines or equivalent. No manual console deployments to production.
Feature store experience — SageMaker Feature Store, Tecton, or Feast — with explicit ownership of online/offline parity.
Champion/challenger, shadow, and canary deployment patterns as production muscle, not blog-post familiarity.
Drift and model monitoring — Evidently, Arize, WhyLabs, or SageMaker Model Monitor — wired to a paging path.
Software-engineering-first mindset — you treat ML systems as systems, not notebooks.
Nice-to-Haves
GenAI in production — Bedrock, Anthropic, or OpenAI APIs integrated into live systems; RAG pipelines; vector DBs (Snowflake Cortex Search, pgvector, Pinecone); evaluation frameworks (Langfuse or in-house).
Snowflake-native ML — Snowpark Container Services, Cortex AISQL, Cortex Agents — for workloads that do not need to leave the warehouse.
Streaming feature engineering — Kafka, Flink, or Snowpipe Streaming — for sub-second features.
Fine-tuning experience — LoRA, QLoRA, instruction tuning, eval-driven iteration — with an honest read on when fine-tuning beats prompting.
A track record of shipping more with AI in the engineering loop than without.
Regulated-industry experience (gaming, fintech, healthcare) — comfort with model risk, audit, and lineage requirements.

Applicants must possess legal authorization to work for our company in the U.S. without the need for immigration sponsorship. At this time, this role is not eligible for immigration-related employment authorization sponsorship including H-1B, O-1, E-3, TN, OPT, etc.

Compensation

The pay range for this position is as follows:

117,100.00--156,200.00

Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate. This position is also eligible for participation in a performance-based bonus plan.

As an online gaming company, BetMGM is required to comply with state gaming regulations which includes licensing obligations. Applicable employees must be licensed by at least one jurisdictional agency, although certain positions require licensing by multiple agencies. Failure to become licensed or maintain licensure with each agency as required for the role may result in termination of employment. Please note that the licensing process includes comprehensive background checks which may include a review of criminal records, financial history, and personal background verification.

In addition, candidates must comply with and support BetMGM's responsible gambling policies, procedures, and initiatives.

BetMGM is revolutionizing sports betting and online gaming in the United States and Canada. We are a partnership between two powerhouse organizations—MGM Resorts International and Entain Group. You know our name through our exciting portfolio of brands including BetMGM Casino, BetMGM Sportsbook, Borgata Online, Party Casino and Party Poker. We aim to bring our ideas into action and find ways to deliver the best quality in gaming platforms.

The Role:

Generate Biomedicines is seeking a principal engineer to lead the evolution of our scientific data and analytical tools. Experimental data is central to how we design, evaluate, and improve protein therapeutics. Making that data accessible, interpretable, and trustworthy is essential to connecting laboratory experimentation with computational design and scientific decision-making.

In this role, you will set the technical direction and deliver systems that connect agents with experimental data, reproducible processing, quality-controlled results, and analysis across experiments. You will help scientists move beyond traditional workflows toward an integrated agentic experience where they can ask questions, explore evidence, and make informed decisions.

You will build on Generate’s agent platform, connecting agents with internal tools, data, and scientific workflows. Working closely with experimental scientists, Data Science, laboratory systems engineers, and the platform team, you will translate scientific needs into a clear roadmap and powerful software. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with responsibility for architecture, implementation, and adoption.

Location:

This role is based in Somerville, MA, with an expectation of working onsite at least three days per week.

Here's how you will contribute:

Define and deliver the scientific data and analytics roadmap. Understand how scientists work today, identify the highest-value opportunities, and turn a broad vision into focused capabilities that improve experimental analysis and decision-making.
Connect the experimental data lifecycle. Design data models, interfaces, and workflows that link raw instrument outputs to samples, experimental conditions, processing methods, QC decisions, and published results. Partner with laboratory systems engineers to establish reliable handoffs from data capture into processing and analysis.
Build reproducible processing and trustworthy results. Work closely with Data Science and assay experts to define and implement mathematical methods, statistical analyses, normalization, and QC rules. Support versioned processing, traceable results, and controlled recomputation as methods evolve.
Create agentic analytical experiences. Build agent-accessible tools and applications that help scientists retrieve data, inspect processing, visualize results, compare experiments, and explore hypotheses. Combine agent flexibility with validated computational methods and appropriate scientific review.
Enable meaningful analysis across experiments. Address differences in assay versions, units, experimental conditions, controls, and sample identity so scientists and computational teams can make defensible comparisons and reuse data.
Lead through implementation and collaboration. Make architectural decisions, build systems, guide engineering contributors, and resolve difficult integration problems. Partner with scientists and program teams to establish requirements, evaluate outputs, and drive adoption.
Own measurable outcomes. Assess success through reliable processing, scientific validity, time saved, and sustained use. Establish practical monitoring and feedback mechanisms, and improve workflows based on real scientific work.

The Ideal Candidate will have:

A bachelor’s or advanced degree in computer science, engineering, bioinformatics, a quantitative scientific discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Substantial experience designing and delivering scientific software or data systems, with demonstrated technical leadership across architecture, implementation, and deployment.
Strong hands-on agentic programming skills, including Python, and experience building data-processing pipelines, APIs, and analytical applications.
Experience developing or integrating AI agents, with sound judgment about their appropriate use, evaluation, and interaction with deterministic processing.
Experience modeling experimental data, including metadata, provenance, versioning, and data quality. Ability to balance consistent structures with the diversity of scientific workflows.
Strong grounding in mathematics, statistics, and experimental analysis to collaborate deeply with data scientists and assay experts and translate their methods into reliable software.
A track record of turning ambiguous scientific needs into a clear technical direction, prioritized deliverables, and software that people use.
Strong collaborative skills and the ability to communicate effectively with experimental scientists, data scientists, software engineers, and scientific leaders.

About Generate Biomedicines

We are a clinical-stage generative biology company pioneering the AI revolution in drug design and development. We are advancing a new approach to drug creation—one grounded in the ability to design proteins with defined biological intent. By integrating machine learning with large-scale experimentation, this approach aims to reduce the uncertainty, time, and cost associated with developing protein-based medicines.

Founded in 2018, we are advancing a growing pipeline of clinical and preclinical programs across multiple disease areas and protein modalities. By unifying computational design and clinical development within a single operating model, we translate this approach into clinical-stage programs and are leading a shift from traditional drug discovery toward systematic drug generation.

At Generate:Biomedicines, we collaborate across disciplines in new ways to invent and innovate. We bring diverse perspectives to a shared goal of delivering better medicines to patients in need, faster, guided by our values and leadership behaviors.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Team Bio:

ServiceNow’s Applied AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE)
team is where bold ideas meet transformative action. We partner with our most strategic customers to shape the future of enterprise AI. Together, we identify high-value opportunities, accelerate business outcomes, and build reusable AI-native solutions that advance the Now AI Platform.

Our mission:
We partner deeply with our customers to build intelligent, scalable AI solutions that solve their most mission-critical challenges. By embedding in real-world complexity, we deliver fast, iterate with purpose, and transform every success into reusable patterns that accelerate transformation across the Now Platform and the broader enterprise.

Why This Role Matters

Enterprises are raising the bar. AI initiatives must deliver business value—not just promise potential. That means taking cutting-edge LLM capabilities and turning them into resilient, secure, and scalable software.

As a Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE)
, you act as the CTO of the build—owning everything from backend services to LLM pipelines and front-end integrations. You partner with customers in the field to design, implement, and deliver solution-ready builds in agile sprints. Your software becomes the reference implementation for scalable GenAI in the enterprise. You codify patterns, shape internal tooling, and accelerate innovation—delivering systems that are battle-tested in production and scalable across industries.

Who You Are

You are a systems-minded, AI-native engineer who ships real software. You own the full stack—and are equally motivated by elegant APIs, intuitive UIs, and scalable orchestration pipelines. You think like a product-minded CTO, balancing creativity with pragmatism to deliver impact.

What You’ll Do

As a GenAI/ML Engineer on the FDE team, you will:

Forward Deployed Engineers sit alongside our customers and turn ambiguous business problems into working AI systems.
Partner directly with customers to discover problems and frame high-impact AI use cases.
Design and build end-to-end GenAI/ML systems — RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, evaluation, and guardrails — and ship them to production.
Prototype quickly, iterate with real users, and harden pilots into reliable, monitored services.
Own the technical relationship, translating between business stakeholders and engineering.
Raise the bar for ML depth and engineering quality across the team.

What Success Looks Like

Production-grade delivery: Your solution builds consistently convert to scaled deployments in production environments
Reusable impact: You author libraries, prompts, and scaffolds that power multiple deployments and projects
Platform influence: Your work shapes internal tooling and is integrated into platform roadmap and primitives
Velocity and precision: You move fast without breaking things—shaping resilient, secure systems in high-stakes contexts
Engineering leadership: You are trusted by architects, PMs, and customer teams to lead implementation from zero to one

Qualifications

What You Bring:

Experience: In leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry
Relevant Experience: 12+ years of software engineering, including 2+ years building systems in customer-facing or embedded roles. Experience building machine learning/ GenAI systems with modern AI/ML technologies, including LLMs, embeddings, vector databases, and RAG architectures.
System architecture: Proven ability to design and implement AI-native software in production environments
Engineering depth: Strength in backend (Python, Node.js, Java), frontend (React, Angular), APIs (REST/GraphQL)
LLM tooling: Familiarity with LangChain, Semantic Kernel, prompt chaining, vector search, and context management
Performance & observability: Skilled in debugging distributed systems, tuning for latency, and implementing monitoring
Platform mindset: Can contribute to shared SDKs and tools, raising engineering velocity for the whole org
Product sensibility: Prioritize for user value, MVP iteration, and long-term scale
DevOps fluency: Experience deploying in AWS, Azure, or GCP with CI/CD, containers, and infra-as-code
Field readiness: Able to travel up to 30% to embed onsite and deliver where it matters

Preferred Qualifications

Experience integrating AI into SaaS platforms like ServiceNow or Salesforce
Track record of production deployments in secure, regulated enterprise environments
Contributions to dev experience tooling, frameworks, or reusable AI scaffolds

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $201,300-$352,300, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs.

Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.
