Overview

Baker Tilly is a leading advisory, tax and assurance firm, providing clients with a genuine coast-to-coast and global advantage in major regions of the U.S. and in many of the world’s leading financial centers – New York, London, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Chicago and Boston. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP (Baker Tilly) provide professional services through an alternative practice structure in accordance with the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct and applicable laws, regulations and professional standards. Baker Tilly US, LLP is a licensed independent CPA firm that provides attest services to its clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities provide tax and business advisory services to their clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities are not licensed CPA firms.

Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP, trading as Baker Tilly, are independent members of Baker Tilly International, a worldwide network of independent accounting and business advisory firms in 141 territories, with 43,000 professionals and a combined worldwide revenue of $5.2 billion. Visit bakertilly.com or join the conversation on LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram.

Please discuss the work location status with your Baker Tilly talent acquisition professional to understand the requirements for an opportunity you are exploring.

Baker Tilly is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable federal, state or local law.

Any unsolicited resumes submitted through our website or to Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, employee e-mail accounts are considered property of Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, and are not subject to payment of agency fees. In order to be an authorized recruitment agency ("search firm") for Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, there must be a formal written agreement in place and the agency must be invited, by Baker Tilly's Talent Attraction team, to submit candidates for review via our applicant tracking system.

Job Description

What we're building

We're building AI agents that do real work for Baker Tilly's tax, assurance, and advisory teams. They read client files, find risks and opportunities, draft financial statement disclosures, and show their sources, and a practitioner always makes the final call. The data is some of the most sensitive in the business, so we build security in from the start.

Baker Tilly is the sixth-largest accounting and advisory firm in the U.S., with more than 11,000 people, and the firm is investing seriously in AI. We're a small team at the start of that work, and the engineers who join now will help decide what we build and how.

As a Principal Full Stack Engineer, you'll be the technical anchor for this team: hands-on, setting the standards for how our agents are built and trusted, and growing the engineers around you. It's an individual-contributor role. You lead with code, judgment, and influence.

What you'll work with

Years of client engagement history, tax returns, and financial records, at the scale of a major firm.
Tax, audit, and advisory practitioners who help define what good looks like and review what the agents produce.
Real users inside the firm who give direct feedback on what you build.
Close collaboration with Ode with Anthropic, an AI engineering company the firm announced an initiative with in July 2026.
A mix of building and buying. You'll help decide which is which, and everything we ship meets the same standards for security, tracing, and testing.
Our stack: Python, TypeScript and React, Databricks, graph and vector databases, MCP, OpenTelemetry, and Braintrust, on Azure.

What you'll do

Set technical direction for a growing set of agents and the data layer underneath them, with secure, well-defined interfaces between them.
Design how agents handle sensitive data: access that follows the person asking, enforced when data is retrieved, with audit records and human approval for what agents create.
Set the bar every agent must meet, whether we build, buy, or integrate it: security, tracing, testing, production readiness. Own how we decide between build and buy.
Write code. Build the high-leverage pieces and take on the hardest production problems yourself.
Make testing a core discipline: expert-labeled ground truth, regression checks, and honest numbers on accuracy, cost, and risk.
Work with product, security, data, legal, and practitioner leaders to settle tradeoffs, and mentor senior engineers through design reviews.
Evaluate models and tools with evidence, and keep humans in the loop where the stakes call for it.
Shape how we ship with AI as we move toward a code factory: the tools, workflows, and standards that keep AI-written code safe in production.

Who you are

You're a hands-on technologist who has built things people actually use, ideally end to end, from the first conversation with users through production and after.
You're naturally curious, a strong problem solver, and a clear communicator.
You can take an objective, form an opinion, and move things forward on your own, and bring others with you, even when the path is unclear.

What you bring

9+ years building and running production software, including complex products you built end to end.
You use AI coding tools extensively, and you have opinions about what works.
Deep experience in a backend language, and the judgment to guide architecture across web, services, APIs, and data.
You've designed systems where access control, data governance, and audit trails were first-class requirements.
You've shipped LLM or agent systems to production, and you have a clear view on evaluation, retrieval, and tool integration.
You explain hard tradeoffs clearly and guide several engineers through them.
You've raised the bar for a team through reusable solutions, good decisions, and mentoring.
A technical degree or equivalent experience.

Nice to have

Shared standards or platforms that several teams adopted.
Databricks or lakehouse architectures, graph and vector databases, MCP, or LLM tracing and evaluation tools.
Evaluating third-party AI vendors against an internal standard, or working with enterprise identity and regulated workflows.

In a year

Every agent we ship, however it's sourced, meets the same bar for safety, tracing, and testing.
Teams make faster, better calls because of patterns you set.
You're still writing code, and other engineers are more independent because of you.

The pay rate range for this job position are listed below. Actual compensation is influenced by a variety of relevant factors including but not limited to applicant’s skills, prior experience, qualifications, degrees, professional certifications, work arrangements and geographic location. Baker Tilly offers a comprehensive compensation and benefits package to eligible employees.

The national pay rate range is $200,000–$350,000

In California: pay rate range is $200,000–$350,000

You will need to be able to confidently articulate our value proposition to leadership, data scientists, developers, and IT teams within the account. This will entail technical architecture walk-throughs, business-value conversations, customer-facing technical workshops, and implementation of best practices in AI systems implementation and design.

You will work closely with the AI business unit and engineering, helping to test, document, and demonstrate cutting-edge features. You will also work in close collaboration with Red Hat customer sales, Customer Success, Consulting Services, and partner teams to ensure a highly positive customer experience.

added.title: AI and Data Science Solution Engineer
added.description:
The Homeland Sensors and Analytics Group designs, builds, and fields solutions that significantly enhance the tactical decision-making process of analysts and operators who secure the homeland. This includes security for critical infrastructure, land and maritime borders, transportation systems, and soft targets / crowded places. It also includes support for law enforcement, special operations, and intelligence analysts who track and disrupt transnational criminal and terrorist organizations. To do this, the group works on a combination of novel sensing technologies and data analytics techniques to provide better threat awareness to decision makers. The group designs systems that collect and process a wide range of data types — including radar, visible imagery and video, non-visible imagery, text, time-series data, and 3D point clouds — often applying advanced machine learning methods to convert raw data into actionable insights. The group places an emphasis on taking technology from the concept phase through deployment and transition to achieve operational impact.

Job Overview

MIT Lincoln Laboratory Associate Technical Staff provide critical multi-domain through expert multi-domain innovative research supporting the Laboratory’s national security mission. They prototype state-of-the-art technology solutions and engage in many steps of a program lifecycle with increasing independence and responsibility. As an Associate Technical Staff member, you will contribute independently to multidisciplinary efforts, contribute to sponsor briefings, write test plans and reports, and apply complex and creative solutions to solving technical problems. You may own discrete project/program components or lead complex workstreams and small teams.

As a successful candidate, you will bring solid to strong technical depth, broaden your understanding across adjacent disciplines, and adapt approaches where precedent is limited. You will integrate technical inputs, contribute to program documentation and reporting, and collaborate with interdisciplinary project/program teams supporting projects that may range from rapid, high-risk efforts to longer-term mission programs. Your work will include multiple activities such as hardware and software development, systems analysis, data analysis, component fabrication, system integration, testing, and documentation.

Additional Job Overview Details

The Homeland Sensors and Analytics group is seeking a researcher and engineer to build software solutions incorporating advanced algorithms, AI/ML, and data science models. This work will be performed as part of collaborative, interdisciplinary teams, with the selected candidate sometimes serving as a task lead. Specifically, the candidate will direct the design, software implementation, and testing of novel algorithms relevant to Homeland Security and Defense applications. Familiarity with AI/ML concepts (including frontier models), graph analytics, statistical models, or data science methods is considered important, as well as experience with the design and implementation of such methods within robust software frameworks. This position will provide the opportunity to learn about mission-relevant applications of data analytics tools, conduct independent research on applicable models and techniques, and enable the deployment of developed solutions to achieve operational impact. The position will also allow the candidate to interface with different agencies and user bases within the US Government, to discuss technical concepts, and present results.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

Own or lead design, development, data analysis, programming, modeling, simulation, integration, testing, troubleshooting, and technical evaluation activities within broader project or program efforts.
Apply technical depth and judgment to less-defined and complex problems, identifying appropriate methods, adapting established approaches, and evaluating trade-offs.
Contribute to or lead system-, subsystem-, or component-level work spanning multiple disciplines, mission needs, products, or technical focus areas.
Develop, review, and integrate technical documentation, analyses, design materials, program reporting, presentations, papers, and other deliverables.
Coordinate milestones, assumptions, dependencies, quality expectations, and risks and present findings, recommendations, and alternatives to appropriate audiences.
Provide technical guidance, review, feedback, and mentorship while continuing to deepen mission-aligned expertise.

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates will be considered for the appropriate level based on their education, experience, demonstrated technical capabilities, leadership responsibilities, and the scope and complexity of their prior work.

Level 3 – Associate Technical Staff

Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline or other relevant technical field and typically 2+ years of relevant experience; or Master’s degree and typically 0+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Solid technical depth in a primary engineering, research, or other technical domain, with the ability to apply knowledge independently.
Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems and manage components of project work.
Experience contributing to technical documentation, analyses, reports, presentations, or project deliverables.
Ability to collaborate across project teams and communicate technical information clearly to appropriate audiences.
Emerging ability to guide less experienced colleagues and contribute to team capability development.

Level 4 – Associate Technical Staff

Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline or other relevant technical field and typically 4+ years of relevant experience; or Master’s degree and typically 2+ years of relevant experience; a PhD may be considered; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Strong technical depth in a primary domain with emerging breadth across related engineering, research, technical disciplines, or mission areas.
Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems and lead components of projects or technical workstreams.
Experience managing milestones, dependencies, risks, and deliverables for assigned project areas.
Ability to communicate complex information to varied audiences and collaborate with project teams, sponsors, and internal partners.
Demonstrated ability to mentor others, review work, and contribute to team technical capability.

Additional Minimum Qualifications

Degree in computer science, mathematics, statistics, electrical engineering, information science, applied mathematics, data science, or an equivalent field.
Knowledge to develop, implement, test, and evaluate algorithms and software
Proficiency with Python
Experience with one or more common machine learning, computer vision, or natural language processing toolboxes
Experience building software systems designed to meet end-user requirements.
Ability to work both in a team-oriented environment and independently.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly share technical concepts with a wide spectrum of audiences.
Experience with some software development best practices and collaboration tools (e.g., github)

Experience In The Following Areas Is Desired

Statistical modeling and inference
Social network analysis
AI/ML models and methods
Collection and analysis of publicly available information
Familiarity with additional programming languages like C++ or Java.
Experience with DevSecOps or CI/CD practices

ConstructConnect is accelerating how AI is applied across our products, platforms, and engineering workflows. We are looking for an AI Engineer to design, build, and operate shared AI capabilities that other engineering teams can use to deliver secure, scalable, production-ready solutions.

In this role, you will partner with software engineering, platform engineering, data, security, and product teams to make AI easier to adopt across the organization through practical services, tooling, and repeatable implementation patterns. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys building production systems, improving developer workflows, and helping turn promising AI concepts into reliable solutions for internal teams and customers.

Responsibilities

What You’ll Be Doing

Platform & Service Development

Design, implement, and maintain shared AI platform components such as services, SDKs, templates, workflows, and reusable libraries that software engineering teams can adopt quickly and safely.
Contribute to engineering patterns and paved paths for AI usage, including model access, prompt handling, evaluation, observability, security, and production support.
Partner with product, application, data, and platform teams to translate AI use cases into scalable technical solutions instead of one-off implementations.
Build and operate reliable, cost-aware AI and ML services on cloud platforms using containerized workloads, managed services, and modern infrastructure practices.
Build and improve internal APIs, developer tooling, and integration patterns that simplify access to AI providers, model endpoints, retrieval services, and supporting data systems.

Operations & Delivery

Support end-to-end workflows for AI and ML use cases, including data preparation, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management.
Contribute to CI/CD practices for AI-enabled services and ML components, including automated quality checks, security controls, and release guardrails.

Troubleshoot and resolve issues related to AI and ML deployments, including latency, scalability, integration failures, reliability problems, and cloud cost concerns.

Governance & Enablement

Partner with security, platform engineering, and architecture teams to ensure AI usage aligns with company policies for data classification, access control, privacy, and compliance.
Evaluate emerging AI technologies, frameworks, and vendor capabilities, and share recommendations on where they may fit within ConstructConnect’s engineering roadmap.
Contribute documentation, runbooks, onboarding materials, and reference implementations that help teams adopt AI capabilities with confidence.
This job description in no way implies that the duties listed here are the only ones that team members can be required to perform.

Required

5–7 years of experience in software engineering, machine learning engineering, platform engineering, or a related area building and operating production systems.
Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language such as Python, Go, or TypeScript, along with solid software design, debugging, and engineering fundamentals.
Experience building and operating services on a major cloud platform, preferably Google Cloud Platform, including familiarity with compute, storage, networking, and managed services.
Hands-on experience with containers and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
Experience with CI/CD pipelines and Git-based engineering workflows used to build, test, and deploy services and platform components.
Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform for provisioning and managing cloud resources in a repeatable, auditable way.

Experience building APIs, services, platforms, or libraries that are consumed by other engineers, with a focus on reliability, usability, and documentation.
Strong foundation in observability and operational excellence, including experience managing service health through metrics, logs, dashboards, and alerting.
Experience working cross-functionally with product, data, infrastructure, platform, and security teams.
Ability to translate technical topics into practical guidance and collaborate effectively in a distributed, remote-friendly environment.

Preferred

Experience with Google Cloud AI and data services such as Vertex AI, BigQuery, or related managed tooling.
Familiarity with AI evaluation frameworks, guardrails, prompt management, model routing, and lifecycle governance.
Experience working with vector search, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, or orchestration frameworks in production settings.
Exposure to intelligent search, recommendation systems, NLP, or computer vision use cases.
Background working in environments where security, governance, and operational reliability are important to AI adoption.

Jumio is looking for a Research Engineer with a foundation in machine learning, robotics, and data infrastructure to help build and scale the systems used for data collection, model development, and product improvement.

This role sits at the intersection of robotics, computer vision, and applied machine learning. You will work hands-on with robotic systems, ROS/ROS2-based modules, mobile data collection workflows, and ML pipelines that support training, evaluation, and production model performance. This is a strong opportunity for a new graduate or early-career engineer who wants to build practical systems that directly improve real-world AI products.

Role Value

High-quality data and reliable model evaluation infrastructure are critical to improving Jumio’s machine learning and computer vision capabilities. This role helps ensure that data collected from robotic systems and mobile applications is usable, scalable, and connected to the broader model development lifecycle.

The Research Engineer will support both the robotics/data collection environment and the ML development workflow, helping the team move faster, improve model quality, and better understand model performance in production.

Build and integrate ROS/ROS2-based modules to support robotic navigation, manipulation, and data collection workflows.

Build, maintain, and improve training and test datasets collected through robotic manipulators and in-house iOS and Android applications.

Collaborate cross-functionally with machine learning, engineering, product, and research teams to improve data collection, model development, and system performance.

Experience working with databases, writing queries, and building or maintaining data pipelines for training, testing, or evaluation.
Strong programming skills in Python and C++, with an emphasis on clean, reliable, well-documented code.

Experience with data collection pipelines for computer vision, biometric systems, identity verification, or similar applied AI domains.

added.title: Research Engineer, Voice AI [NYC or SF]
added.description:
About Concurrence

Concurrence (formerly Amigo) is building the platform healthcare organizations use to build their own clinical AI agents. Our mission is to make excellent care accessible to every patient, not rationed by the limits of clinician time.

Underneath our platform is the Health World Model, which unifies a health system’s data into a living, event-level record of every patient’s care. On top of it, agents handle work across the patient journey, from intake and scheduling to medication management and clinical decision support.

Our agents have supported more than 10 million patient encounters and are on track to grow tenfold this year. We run natively on Databricks, integrate with every major EHR, and are backed by Madrona, General Catalyst, and Optum Ventures. We’re about 35 people, working in person in New York and San Francisco.

About This Role

As a Research Engineer, Voice AI at Concurrence, you'll build and tune speech models for patient conversations and ambient clinical audio. You'll own models from data and training through evaluation and production, working with runtime engineers on streaming inference, latency and turn-taking. The work includes full-duplex speech-to-speech models that listen and speak at the same time, handle interruptions and preserve clinical details.

What You'll Do

Train and fine-tune speech and audio models for patient calls and clinical encounters
Own data preparation, training experiments and evaluation code
Improve streaming inference, turn-taking and interruption handling, balancing model quality, latency and cost
Define clinical failure cases with clinicians, product and evaluation engineers, and measure the errors that matter to patients
Evaluate changes on held-out examples, investigate regressions and carry improvements into production
Use evidence from real conversations to choose the next experiment and shape our modeling approach

What we're looking for

You've personally trained or fine-tuned speech or audio models on large audio datasets as a substantial part of your work
You've shipped a model into a real-time product, with concrete results on streaming inference, latency, turn-taking or overlapping speech
You've taken an ambiguous problem, defined a useful metric and led the work through to a model running in production
You write the training and evaluation code yourself and can explain the choices behind an experiment
You use coding agents in your work and independently verify their output
You're low ego, direct, and hold yourself to a high bar
You can work on site in New York City or San Francisco

Nice to have

Experience building or tuning a full-duplex speech-to-speech model, our strongest preference
Neural audio codecs or audio language models
Telephone audio, overlapping speech or multi-speaker audio
Model adaptation for a particular customer, domain or regulated environment

Benefits (available To Full-Time Employees)

Health & Wellness

Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
Daily catered lunch and dinner
Mental health support and wellness coaching
Flexible wellness stipend for fitness, therapy, or personal growth

Growth & Development

Annual learning budget for courses, books, or conferences
Conference attendance budget for professional development
Annual team offsite
Academic collaboration opportunities
Unlimited PTO

Our Core Values

Patients Win, We Win

If patients aren't getting better care, we haven't earned the right to scale. Every internal decision gets pressure-tested: does this make patients' lives better? If we can't draw the line, we question why we're doing it.

High Standards, High Care

We hold a high bar for the team because patients are counting on us to get this right. But high standards only work with genuine investment in each other. You can take risks, admit mistakes, and challenge ideas. Not despite our standards, but because of them.

Thoughtful Urgency

We move fast by default, but speed without judgment is recklessness. The discipline is knowing which decisions are reversible vs. not. In healthcare AI, the companies that win will be fast everywhere they can be and careful everywhere they must be. We build the muscle to do both.

Intensely Measured

We instrument patient outcomes, provider ROI, system performance, and clinical accuracy. But data without action is surveillance. Every metric should have an owner, a threshold, and a response plan. If we're measuring something but never acting on it, we stop measuring it. Who Builds With Us

Low ego: Politics and territory don't interest you. The best ideas win, regardless of who has them.
Direct: You say the hard thing, challenge ideas openly, and commit fully once decided.
High agency: You thrive on trust rather than instruction. When you see something is broken, you fix it. You don’t file tickets and wait for someone else.
Bar of excellence: You hold yourself to a bar most people wouldn't, and you want teammates who do the same.
Skeptical: You push back on rules that don’t make sense and question assumptions that haven’t earned their place.

Compensation Range: $220K - $300K

Core Capabilities

Why Join iCatalyst?

At iCatalyst, our people are at the center of everything we do.

Award-winning culture of innovation and a friendly workplace
Work on cutting-edge AI and digital transformation projects

Grow your career in a stable, certified, high-performing organization

added.title: Forward Deployment Engineer
added.description:
At T-Mobile, we invest in YOU! Our Total Rewards Package ensures that employees get the same big love we give our customers. All team members receive a competitive base salary and compensation package - this is Total Rewards. Employees enjoy multiple wealth-building opportunities through our annual stock grant, employee stock purchase plan, 401(k), and access to free, year-round money coaches. That’s how we’re UNSTOPPABLE for our employees!

Are you ready to join the Un-carrier movement?

The Engineer, Forward Deployment is a hands-on technical practitioner who embeds within a T-Mobile business unit to design, build, and iterate on net-new agentic AI solutions. These solutions are developed against requirements defined and scoped by TPMs and business unit stakeholders. Forward Deployment Engineers (FDEs) write code, run experiments, debug production systems, and work closely with business unit stakeholder teams to deliver AI solutions that achieve stated business outcomes.

FDEs typically work alongside a Senior FDE who owns the domain relationship and sets technical direction. The Engineer is responsible for the execution layer: building system integrations, tuning prompts, running A/B cohorts, and delivering against validated ROI targets for the domain. Performance is measured by contribution to validated return on investment outcomes for each domain assignment — not by activity or ticket volume. This role reports to the Manager or Senior Manager, Forward Deployment Engineer within the assigned pod.

We pride ourselves on fostering a culture of innovation, advocating for agile methodologies, and promoting transparency in all that we do. Join us in embodying the spirit of the 'Un-carrier' and make a tangible impact! If you're up to the challenge, apply today!

Job Responsibilities:

AI System Deployment & Tuning: Implement, configure, and iteratively tune net-new agentic AI solutions deployed in the assigned business domain, working against requirements defined and delivered by TPMs. Adapt solution behavior, prompt layers, and escalation logic based on live operational feedback on a weekly cycle.
A/B Experimentation & ROI Validation: Run controlled A/B experiments in live production cohorts and document measured impact on validated return on investment targets for the domain. Feed results back to the FDE team and practice leadership with structured analysis to inform delivery prioritization.
BU Partnership & Workflow Engagement: Work directly alongside BU teams in the assigned domain across care, retail, finance, supply chain, or other operational contexts. Observe real workflows, identify friction that AI solutions can address, and conduct structured feedback sessions with BU managers and end users.
Data Engineering & System Integrations: Build system integrations connecting AI solutions to BU data sources such as CRM, billing, ticketing, and ERP platforms. Prepare and normalize business-unit-specific data for AI system consumption. Build lightweight ETL pipelines feeding operational data into evaluation loops and monitoring dashboards. Identify and escalate data quality gaps with specific documentation.
Practice Reporting & Requirements Support: Contribute to reporting cycles that support the TPM-defined requirements pipeline. Document system performance, failure modes, and gaps in a structured format that supports domain planning and delivery prioritization. Participate in practice reviews to share domain learnings.
Contributes structured documentation: failure modes, edge cases, performance gaps, and develops them into practice reporting cycles.
Participates in rotation planning and knowledge transfer sessions.
Contributes to peer knowledge sharing
Supports onboarding of rotating FDEs at the IC level.
Implements integrations and data normalization pipelines for assigned BU data sources. Flags data quality issues and raises to Sr. FDE or TPM.
Builds and iterates on assigned components of agentic systems, individual agents, RAG pipelines, prompt layers, while under architectural direction.
Delivers A/B experiments and documents results.

Education and Work Experience:

Highly Desired: Current or recent experience as a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) within the startup ecosystem, preferably in a fast-paced, high-growth technology or AI-focused company, with demonstrated experience delivering customer-facing technical solutions.
Bachelor's Degree Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or related technical field. Relevant equivalent experience accepted. (Required)
2-4+ years hands-on software or ML engineering experience in production environments. Demonstrated ability to write clean, maintainable Python code and to debug and extend existing codebases. Experience deploying to cloud environments and building system integrations with enterprise data sources. (Required)
4-7+ years prior experience in a customer-facing, operations, or embedded technical role (care, retail, finance, supply chain). Exposure to enterprise AI platforms such as Salesforce Einstein, ServiceNow AI, or Microsoft Copilot. (Preferred)

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Python Engineering: Python proficiency in production settings: clean, maintainable code; able to read, debug, and extend existing agentic system code written by others.
LLM Integration: Working knowledge of LLM integration patterns: prompt engineering, RAG basics, function calling; experience with at least one major LLM provider.
Data Engineering & System Integrations: SQL proficiency; experience building system integrations connecting AI solutions to enterprise data sources (CRM, ticketing, ERP, billing); able to build lightweight ETL/ELT pipelines and instrument systems with basic logging.
Cloud & DevOps Literacy: Comfortable deploying to AWS or Azure, using Docker, and reading CI/CD pipelines.
Operational Bias to Action: Ships iterative improvements in days, not weeks; able to communicate technical trade-offs clearly to non-technical partners.
Data Security & Responsible AI: Solid understanding of data privacy requirements in enterprise environments including PII and customer data protection. Applies responsible AI principles and appropriate data handling practices when building system integrations and AI solutions.
Forward Deployment Mentality: Demonstrated ability to embed within a business unit, earn stakeholder trust rapidly, and deliver working AI systems under real operational constraints, not in sandbox or lab environments.
Stakeholder Translation: Ability to move fluidly between technical implementation and business communication, converting engineering tradeoffs into plain-language impact narratives for BU managers, and converting vague business asks into precise engineering requirements.
Rapid Prototyping & Production Readiness: Experience compressing the gap between proof-of-concept and production-grade delivery.
At least 18 years of age
Legally authorized to work in the United States

Travel
:

Travel Required (Yes/No): Yes

DOT Regulated
:

DOT Regulated Position (Yes/No): No

Safety Sensitive Position (Yes/No): No

To learn about T-Mobile’s amazing benefits, check out www.t-mobilebenefits.com .

Never stop growing!

We love helping our employees grow in their careers, because it’s that shared drive to aim high that drives our business and our culture forward. added.title: Agentic AI Engineer
added.description:
AI Engineering | Forward Deployed Engineering

Role Description

Defense Unicorns is seeking an Agentic Engineer to embed with a government team and its technology partners building an emerging AI-powered engineering ecosystem.

This role will focus on designing, integrating, and operationalizing AI agents and agentic workflows within a secure enterprise environment. The engineer will work across large language models, agent frameworks, enterprise data, APIs, developer tooling, and platform services to turn AI capabilities into reliable, mission-relevant workflows.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who understands both the capabilities and limitations of modern AI systems and can rapidly translate emerging technologies into working solutions. They should be comfortable experimenting with new models and agent frameworks, integrating agents with enterprise systems and tools, evaluating performance and reliability, and working alongside platform engineers and commercial technology partners.

This is not a research-only role. The focus is on moving from AI concepts and prototypes to secure, useful, repeatable agentic capabilities that can operate in production environments.

Responsibilities

Design, build, and integrate AI agents and multi-agent workflows using modern LLM and agentic technologies.
Develop agent capabilities that interact with enterprise applications, APIs, data sources, developer tools, and mission systems.
Integrate models, agents, tools, and enterprise data into secure workflows that can be deployed in controlled and classified environments.
Work with LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector databases, tool/function calling, structured outputs, MCP, and related technologies.
Develop mechanisms for agents to securely discover, access, reason over, and act upon approved enterprise data and services.
Prototype and rapidly evaluate emerging models, agent frameworks, and AI capabilities to determine where they can create measurable mission or engineering value.
Develop evaluation and testing frameworks for agent accuracy, reliability, safety, latency, cost, and task completion.
Implement guardrails and policy controls governing agent behavior, tool access, data access, and human approval points.
Integrate agentic capabilities with CI/CD and DevSecOps workflows to support repeatable development, testing, deployment, and lifecycle management.
Collaborate with platform engineers to operationalize AI workloads within Kubernetes/OpenShift environments.
Work with commercial AI and technology partners to integrate their capabilities into the broader engineering ecosystem.
Troubleshoot issues across models, agent frameworks, APIs, data sources, networking, identity, and infrastructure.
Develop reusable patterns for agent deployment, configuration, observability, evaluation, and lifecycle management.
Document architectures, integration patterns, agent specifications, evaluation results, and operational procedures.
Identify recurring AI engineering challenges that can be standardized, automated, or productized into reusable capabilities.
Stay current with rapidly evolving agentic AI technologies and assess their applicability to secure government environments.

Minimum Experience And Qualifications

Active Top Secret clearance.
2-5 years of Hands-on experience building applications or systems using large language models and generative AI.
Experience designing and implementing AI agents or agentic workflows.
Strong programming experience in Python and/or another modern programming language.
Experience integrating AI systems with APIs, enterprise applications, databases, and external tools.
Experience with one or more agent frameworks or orchestration approaches.
Working knowledge of RAG, embeddings, vector databases, tool/function calling, structured outputs, and prompt engineering.
Experience developing software in a Git-based, automated CI/CD environment.
Ability to rapidly prototype, test, troubleshoot, and iterate in ambiguous environments.
Strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including testing, version control, APIs, debugging, and system design.
Ability to work effectively alongside platform engineers, government personnel, and multiple technology vendors.

Preferred Experience And Qualifications

Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and tool-based agent architectures.
Experience with multi-agent systems and agent orchestration.
Experience with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, NVIDIA, or comparable foundation model ecosystems.
Experience with NVIDIA NIM, NeMo, or similar AI inference/model-serving technologies.
Experience with Red Hat OpenShift AI or Kubernetes-based AI platforms.
Experience with agent evaluation and observability frameworks.
Experience implementing AI guardrails, policy enforcement, human-in-the-loop workflows, or AI safety controls.
Experience with LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or comparable frameworks.
Experience with RAG pipelines, vector databases, knowledge graphs, and enterprise search.
Experience deploying AI systems in Secret or TS/SCI environments.
Experience with disconnected or air-gapped AI environments.
Experience integrating AI into developer/DevSecOps workflows.
Familiarity with GitLab, Jira, Confluence, Xacta, or similar enterprise engineering and compliance tools.
Experience working with GPUs, model serving, inference optimization, or AI infrastructure.
Familiarity with UDS, Zarf, Pepr, Iron Bank, or similar secure software delivery technologies.
Experience taking AI prototypes into repeatable, production-ready capabilities.
Ability to evaluate new AI technologies quickly and make pragmatic build/buy/integrate decisions.

What Success Looks Like

Agentic capabilities move from prototype to mission use quickly, with working agents integrated into real government workflows rather than remaining isolated demos.
Agents reliably connect to approved enterprise data, tools, and services, with appropriate identity, permissions, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls.
AI capabilities are measurable and trustworthy, with repeatable evaluation methods for accuracy, reliability, task completion, security, and operational performance.
Reusable agent patterns emerge, reducing the engineering required to build and deploy the next agent or AI-enabled workflow.
AI integrates cleanly with the broader platform architecture, working effectively across the data, DevSecOps, Kubernetes/OpenShift, model, and application layers rather than creating another technology silo.
The engineer becomes a trusted AI technical advisor to the Mission Hero, proactively identifying where agentic technology can create mission value—and equally important, where AI is not the right solution.

Full compensation packages are based on candidate experience. Compensation ranges are established using national benchmarking data and apply across all geographic locations within the United States.

Remote - USA

$148,750—$201,250 USD

Who We Are

Defense Unicorns delivers mission value by streamlining software delivery so our customers can focus on the most important challenges. We share a vision of freedom and security for the advancement of progress and innovation. Our commitment to this vision, and to our mission-driven customers, means a commitment to speed, user experience and optionality, without compromising security. Our team is composed of innovators, software engineers, and veterans with decades of experience delivering technology programs across the federal market.

What We Do

We create and deliver secure solutions for continuous software integration and delivery. Defense Unicorns consolidates the best practices for security pipelines, testing, and deployment automation in order to meet the high security requirements valued by mission owners. Our solutions are agnostic by design and we believe that growing a robust ecosystem of secure, cloud-native software solutions can help enterprise customers inside and outside the federal market buy and integrate software more easily.

added.description:
About Fundbox

Small businesses are the backbone of the American economy, but they're constantly constrained by cash flow. We're changing that.

At Fundbox, we're building embedded lending infrastructure that delivers unsecured working capital to small businesses at the exact moment they need it: fast, intuitive, and built into the software they already use. We partner with industry-leading platforms to make financial access feel invisible.

This is mission-driven work with real impact. Every system you build helps a small business grow, hire, and thrive. We're scaling our US engineering presence as part of a global team, and this is your chance to get in early and shape how we build.

The Role

We're looking for a software engineer who followed the data. You built serious production services first (APIs, distributed systems, things that had to stay up), then moved into data engineering or ML infrastructure because that's where the hard problems were. Now you want a role that uses both halves.

At Fundbox, credit decisions are made by models, and those models are only as good as the systems around them. You'll build the services that power our lending products and partner integrations, and you'll build the pipelines, feature serving, and deployment paths that put our ML models into those same services in real time. This isn't a role where models get thrown over a wall; you'll own the path from feature to decision.

What makes this role different

Both sides of the wall:
You'll write product backend code and ML platform code in the same quarter, often in the same system. Few roles let you do both seriously.
Models that move money:
Our models decide who gets capital and on what terms. Latency, correctness, and reliability have real financial consequences.
Close to the people who use your work:
Data scientists and our risk team rely on the features and pipelines you build. You'll be their go-to partner for questions about how features work, where data comes from, and why a number looks the way it does.
Global collaboration:
You'll work closely with the core platform team in Tel Aviv, plus engineers in Tbilisi: different perspectives, follow-the-sun development, a truly distributed engineering culture.
Early-stage influence:
You'll get architectural ownership earlier than you would at a big tech company, with direct influence on how our ML and data platform evolves as we scale.

What you'll build

Product backend

Credit infrastructure:
Services for real-time credit evaluation, underwriting, and decisioning, where model outputs become lending decisions.
Partner integrations:
APIs that let software platforms embed Fundbox, and the data flows that come back from them.
Financial products:
Lending products like term loans, lines of credit, and merchant cash advances, and the application, approval, servicing, and repayment flows behind them.

ML and data platform

Feature pipelines:
Robust, scalable systems for feature engineering that serve both online (real-time) and offline (training and batch) inference, with consistency between the two.
Model deployment and serving:
Reliable paths for taking models from a data scientist's notebook into low-latency production services.
CI/CD for models:
Pipelines that support continuous model updates, versioning, and safe rollouts and rollbacks.
Monitoring:
Logging and alerting that catch data drift, model performance issues, and pipeline failures before they reach a credit decision.
Support for data science and risk:
Work with data scientists to develop and refine features, and be the first stop for questions from data science and the risk team about feature definitions, data lineage, and model inputs. When the same question comes up twice, you improve the docs or tooling so it doesn't come up a third time.
Core platform partnership:
Work with the core platform team in Tel Aviv on shared services and infrastructure, and with DevOps and DataOps to fit ML into our broader AWS stack.

What we're looking for

Engineering culture

We hire people we trust and give them autonomy to do great work. High ownership, low micromanagement: you'll own your domain and make decisions without someone looking over your shoulder. Independence doesn't mean isolation; we help each other succeed through thoughtful code reviews and knowledge sharing. High integrity, no politics, no BS. We move fast but we're not a burnout culture.

to their work

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Radar ML team builds the machine learning systems that power Stripe’s Radar fraud and abuse product suite. Our models make real-time decisions across a significant share of internet commerce - helping businesses stop fraud, increase authorization, and grow safely. By turning economy-scale datasets into compelling ML products, the team directly improves customer outcomes and drives meaningful revenue for Stripe.

The team is growing, and expanding into multiple new areas. We are building abuse protections across the full customer life-cycle, adaptive and customizable fraud systems for enterprises, and risk intelligence for 50+ global payment methods.

What you’ll do

You will own ML problems from conception to production: analyzing new fraud and abuse patterns, exploring large-scale datasets, experimenting with model architectures, designing evaluations, deploying models, and monitoring performance.

Your work may include developing transformer architectures for payment data, building graph-powered intelligence across consumers, leveraging LLMs to detect emerging attacks, or rapidly prototyping new protections with frontier AI labs.

You will have opportunities to ship 0→1 products, and to improve mission-critical ML models operating at Stripe scale.

Responsibilities

Build, train, evaluate, and deploy models that detect fraud and abuse across Stripe’s global network.
Investigate emerging fraud and abuse patterns, identify where ML can help, and rapidly develop effective solutions.
Design features, datasets, evaluation methods, and experiments for noisy, delayed, and adversarial environments.
Improve model architectures, training methods, and production systems to increase model quality, coverage, and adaptability.
Monitor production behavior and improve models as data, customer needs, and attack patterns change.
Balance model quality with legitimate-user impact, latency, reliability, and operational complexity.
Partner with engineering, product, data science, risk experts, and leading Stripe users to turn modeling improvements into differentiated Radar products.
Contribute to reusable tools and AI-assisted workflows that help the team develop and operate ML systems more effectively.

Who you are

You are a fast, pragmatic problem solver with deep ML expertise and a bias toward action. You are excited to work at the frontier of payments and AI - turning advances in machine learning into production systems that address new forms of fraud and abuse. You’ve built ML models and shepherded them to production, landing impact for users.

Strong programming and software-engineering skills, with experience writing tested, maintainable code for production ML applications.
Experience building or operating production ML systems, including one or more of large-scale data and feature pipelines, distributed model training, low-latency inference, model deployment, or production monitoring.
Ability to investigate ambiguous problems, reason from data, and choose pragmatic technical approaches.
Ability to communicate technical ideas and results clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience owning an ML problem across the full lifecycle, from problem framing and data exploration through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
Experience developing or productionizing modern deep learning, graph-learning, or LLM-based approaches.
Experience building and optimizing real-time, low-latency ML systems at scale.
Experience applying ML to fraud detection, integrity, trust and safety, identity, cybersecurity, or another adversarial domain.

Active interest in the latest ML developments, and how they can be leveraged to solve business problems.

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Design, build, and deploy production grade LLM applications, RAG pipelines, and agentic workflows using Python and cloud platforms such as Azure and AWS
Act as technical lead for the team: plan and divide technical work, set coding and design standards, and review the code and designs of AI Engineers
Coach and mentor AI Engineers through pairing, design reviews, and regular feedback
Make and document architecture and build vs. buy recommendations for models, platforms, and vendors, balancing cost, speed, quality, and risk

Define where human in the loop control is needed and design review and approval steps for high risk actions
Translate business problems into technical designs, and explain to management and stakeholders what is feasible, what it costs, and what value it delivers
Partner with InfoSec, infrastructure, data, and business teams to move proofs of concept into production and drive adoption
Track emerging AI models, tools, and methods, and advise the Director, AI Implementation on what to adopt and when

DATA SCIENCE RESPONSIBILITIES

Explore, clean, and analyze large structured and unstructured data sets to find patterns, root causes, and opportunities for AI and automation
Build, validate, and deploy machine learning and statistical models (forecasting, classification, regression, anomaly detection) for operational use cases such as capacity, power, and cooling planning
Design experiments and success metrics (baselines, A/B tests, KPIs) to prove the business value of AI solutions before and after go live
Lead feature engineering, model selection, and model validation, and monitor production models for drift and loss of performance
Combine classical machine learning with generative AI where it fits, for example using LLMs to structure text data that feeds predictive models
Turn analysis results into clear insights, dashboards, and recommendations for technical and business audiences
Work with data engineering to make sure data pipelines, data quality, and data governance meet the needs of AI and analytics systems

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

7+ years of practical experience in software engineering, data science, or machine learning, including 3+ years building and running production ML / AI systems OR MS degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or equivalent with 5+ years of experience
2+ years acting as technical lead for engineers or data scientists: setting direction, reviewing work, and mentoring
Expert Python skills for production code, including testing, CI/CD, API design, and asynchronous patterns
Deep experience with generative AI and LLMs: RAG, prompt engineering, tool / function calling, AI agents, and evaluation at scale

Strong SQL and data modeling skills
Strong verbal / written communication skills, including presenting to executive level stakeholders

Experience with time series forecasting and anomaly detection on sensor, telemetry, or IoT data
Experience with fine tuning and model customization (SFT, LoRA) and self hosted inference (e.g., vLLM, Ollama)
Experience with data platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake, or Microsoft Fabric, and BI tools such as Power BI
Experience with ML lifecycle and LLM observability tooling (e.g., MLflow, Azure Machine Learning, LangSmith, Langfuse)
Professional level cloud AI or data science certification (e.g., Microsoft Azure AI Engineer Associate, Azure Data Scientist Associate, AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer)

Familiarity with responsible AI frameworks and regulation (e.g., NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act)

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

added.title: Senior Applied AI Researcher/Engineer for ISRT Intelligent Systems
added.description:
Description

Do you enjoy providing technical leadership, mentoring researchers and engineers, and translating advances in artificial intelligence into robust, mission-relevant capabilities?

Are you interested in shaping innovative approaches in computer vision, deep learning, foundation models, and agentic AI that exploit data from multiple sensors and sources?

Do you want to advance US defense capabilities in Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance, and Targeting (ISRT)?

If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL!

We are seeking a creative and expert Senior Applied AI Researcher/Engineer to lead efforts to conceptualize, develop, test, assess, and field the next generation of ISRT and Counter-ISRT capabilities for the US military. Our team combines an understanding of the physical processes being sensed with advanced methods of signal and image processing, sensor and data fusion, operations research, and artificial intelligence to build systems that make intelligent inferences and predictions about complex threats and environments. Our work enables the US military to neutralize a wider variety of serious threats from safer distances than they could otherwise accomplish; improves the safety, survivability, and effectiveness of US air, naval, and ground forces; and disrupts the ability of potential adversaries to threaten our forces.

As a Senior Applied AI Researcher/Engineer for ISRT Intelligent Systems…

Your primary responsibility will be to lead and contribute to multidisciplinary teams researching, developing, and transitioning AI/ML algorithms and prototype software for complex ISRT applications.
You will establish technical approaches and guide model design, adaptation, training, evaluation, and integration across areas such as computer vision, neural networks, transformers, large language models, and multimodal learning.
You will architect AI-enabled systems that exploit imagery and other sensor data, integrate information across sources, and, where appropriate, use retrieval-augmented generation, intelligent agents, and tool-based workflows.
You will define rigorous experimentation and evaluation strategies, establish meaningful performance metrics, and assess model robustness, generalization, uncertainty, explainability, and operational limitations.
You will lead the maturation of research prototypes into well-engineered capabilities, balancing technical performance, computational constraints, integration risks, and mission requirements.
You will help develop new research directions and proposals, translate sponsor needs into executable technical plans, and guide technical priorities, schedules, and deliverables.
You will mentor junior researchers and engineers, review technical work, and foster sound research, software engineering, and responsible AI practices.
You will lead technical communications with project leadership and government sponsors and present team results through briefings, reports, publications, and technical forums.

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...

Have a Master’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, data science, or another related technical field.
Have at least seven years of relevant professional experience in AI/ML research, algorithm development, applied data science, or intelligent software systems.
Have demonstrated technical depth in one or more modern AI/ML areas such as computer vision, deep neural networks, transformers, large language models, multimodal learning, or agentic AI, with the ability to evaluate and select appropriate approaches.
Have significant hands-on experience using Python and modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Hugging Face Transformers to develop, train, adapt, and evaluate models.
Have a record of leading complex technical efforts, guiding multidisciplinary teams, and delivering research or prototype capabilities with measurable results.
Have participated as a principal investigator, key contributor, or key advisor on an internal or external research proposal that was funded.
Have experience designing technically rigorous experiments, interpreting results, and communicating tradeoffs and limitations to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Have strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills and the ability to mentor staff, support concurrent projects, and adapt to evolving priorities.
Are willing and able to work a portion of the time in secure, closed areas and travel occasionally to government sites and contractor facilities (local and non-local).
Are able to obtain an Interim Secret level security clearance by your start date and can ultimately a TS/SCI level clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.

You'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you...

Have a Doctorate degree in a related technical field.
Have demonstrated experience leading applied research involving vision-language models, multimodal sensor fusion, LLM adaptation/evaluation, or agentic AI and multi-agent systems.
Have experience with ISR sensor data, remote sensing, computer vision for imagery exploitation, tracking, sensor/data fusion, or autonomous decision-support systems.
Have experience transitioning AI/ML research into operational or production-relevant systems, including scalable inference, deployment constraints, model monitoring, and repeatable evaluation.
Have experience developing funded research concepts, shaping sponsor-facing technical roadmaps, or serving as a principal investigator or technical lead.
Have familiarity with trustworthy and responsible AI, including reliability, uncertainty, explainability, human-machine teaming, and evaluation under distribution shift.
Hold an active Secret, Top Secret, or TS/SCI-level security clearance.

The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) brings world-class expertise to our nation’s most critical defense, security, space and science challenges. While we are dedicated to solving complex challenges and pioneering new technologies, what makes us truly outstanding is our culture. We offer a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere where you can bring your authentic self to work, continue to grow, and build strong connections with inspiring teammates.

added.title: Principal Software Engineer, Applied AI
added.description:
The Role:

Generate Biomedicines is seeking a principal engineer to lead the evolution of our scientific data and analytical tools. Experimental data is central to how we design, evaluate, and improve protein therapeutics. Making that data accessible, interpretable, and trustworthy is essential to connecting laboratory experimentation with computational design and scientific decision-making.

In this role, you will set the technical direction and deliver systems that connect agents with experimental data, reproducible processing, quality-controlled results, and analysis across experiments. You will help scientists move beyond traditional workflows toward an integrated agentic experience where they can ask questions, explore evidence, and make informed decisions.

You will build on Generate’s agent platform, connecting agents with internal tools, data, and scientific workflows. Working closely with experimental scientists, Data Science, laboratory systems engineers, and the platform team, you will translate scientific needs into a clear roadmap and powerful software. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with responsibility for architecture, implementation, and adoption.

Location:

This role is based in Somerville, MA, with an expectation of working onsite at least three days per week.

Here's how you will contribute:

Define and deliver the scientific data and analytics roadmap. Understand how scientists work today, identify the highest-value opportunities, and turn a broad vision into focused capabilities that improve experimental analysis and decision-making.
Connect the experimental data lifecycle. Design data models, interfaces, and workflows that link raw instrument outputs to samples, experimental conditions, processing methods, QC decisions, and published results. Partner with laboratory systems engineers to establish reliable handoffs from data capture into processing and analysis.
Build reproducible processing and trustworthy results. Work closely with Data Science and assay experts to define and implement mathematical methods, statistical analyses, normalization, and QC rules. Support versioned processing, traceable results, and controlled recomputation as methods evolve.
Create agentic analytical experiences. Build agent-accessible tools and applications that help scientists retrieve data, inspect processing, visualize results, compare experiments, and explore hypotheses. Combine agent flexibility with validated computational methods and appropriate scientific review.
Enable meaningful analysis across experiments. Address differences in assay versions, units, experimental conditions, controls, and sample identity so scientists and computational teams can make defensible comparisons and reuse data.
Lead through implementation and collaboration. Make architectural decisions, build systems, guide engineering contributors, and resolve difficult integration problems. Partner with scientists and program teams to establish requirements, evaluate outputs, and drive adoption.
Own measurable outcomes. Assess success through reliable processing, scientific validity, time saved, and sustained use. Establish practical monitoring and feedback mechanisms, and improve workflows based on real scientific work.

The Ideal Candidate will have:

A bachelor’s or advanced degree in computer science, engineering, bioinformatics, a quantitative scientific discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Substantial experience designing and delivering scientific software or data systems, with demonstrated technical leadership across architecture, implementation, and deployment.
Strong hands-on agentic programming skills, including Python, and experience building data-processing pipelines, APIs, and analytical applications.
Experience developing or integrating AI agents, with sound judgment about their appropriate use, evaluation, and interaction with deterministic processing.
Experience modeling experimental data, including metadata, provenance, versioning, and data quality. Ability to balance consistent structures with the diversity of scientific workflows.
Strong grounding in mathematics, statistics, and experimental analysis to collaborate deeply with data scientists and assay experts and translate their methods into reliable software.
A track record of turning ambiguous scientific needs into a clear technical direction, prioritized deliverables, and software that people use.
Strong collaborative skills and the ability to communicate effectively with experimental scientists, data scientists, software engineers, and scientific leaders.

About Generate Biomedicines

We are a clinical-stage generative biology company pioneering the AI revolution in drug design and development. We are advancing a new approach to drug creation—one grounded in the ability to design proteins with defined biological intent. By integrating machine learning with large-scale experimentation, this approach aims to reduce the uncertainty, time, and cost associated with developing protein-based medicines.

Founded in 2018, we are advancing a growing pipeline of clinical and preclinical programs across multiple disease areas and protein modalities. By unifying computational design and clinical development within a single operating model, we translate this approach into clinical-stage programs and are leading a shift from traditional drug discovery toward systematic drug generation.

At Generate:Biomedicines, we collaborate across disciplines in new ways to invent and innovate. We bring diverse perspectives to a shared goal of delivering better medicines to patients in need, faster, guided by our values and leadership behaviors.

added.description:
About SecurityScorecard:

SecurityScorecard is the global leader in cybersecurity ratings, with over 12 million companies continuously rated, operating in 64 countries. Founded in 2013 by security and risk experts Dr. Alex Yampolskiy and Sam Kassoumeh and funded by world-class investors, SecurityScorecard’s patented rating technology is used by over 25,000 organizations for self-monitoring, third-party risk management, board reporting, and cyber insurance underwriting; making all organizations more resilient by allowing them to easily find and fix cybersecurity risks across their digital footprint.

Headquartered in New York City, our culture has been recognized by Inc Magazine as a "Best Workplace,” by Crain’s NY as a "Best Places to Work in NYC," and as one of the 10 hottest SaaS startups in New York for two years in a row. Most recently, SecurityScorecard was named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2023 and to the Achievers 50 Most Engaged Workplaces in 2023 award recognizing “forward-thinking employers for their unwavering commitment to employee engagement.” SecurityScorecard is proud to be funded by world-class investors including Silver Lake Waterman, Moody’s, Sequoia Capital, GV and Riverwood Capital.

About the Role:

We're starting a new engineering team, and its job is to change how SecurityScorecard builds software. You'll be one of the first people on it.

The team works out how a company our size should ship code now that agents can write most of it. That means real work on the codebase: running agentic coding workflows end to end, finding where they break, building the tooling and guardrails that fix those breaks, and turning what works into the way the rest of engineering operates. We'll pick product areas to test against as we go. Over time the team takes on real product ownership and folds back into the wider engineering org.

We want strong engineers who went deep on AI coding because they couldn't leave it alone. You know how production systems fail and you've pushed agentic tools far enough to know where they still fall short. You also care about building a team you'd want to work on, and you'll stick around after the novelty wears off.

This is greenfield. You'll report to our CTO or to an engineer leading the team, and the reporting lines will move as the team grows. If titles and org charts matter a lot to you, this role won't be a good fit. We care about execution and impact.

What you'll do

Run agentic coding workflows on production code and find out what actually holds up at our scale
Build the tooling, guardrails, evals and review practices that let agents ship code we trust
Design systems that stay sound when most of the code is written by agents, and decide where humans need to stay in the loop
Ship real changes to our products, using them as test cases for the new way of working
Pair with engineers across the org, review their work and help them adopt what we learn
Raise the hiring bar: interview candidates and help decide who joins the team
Write down what we learn so other teams can use it without us in the room
Design, build, and ship customer-facing AI-powered product features using TypeScript, Go, and AWS, owning quality and reliability end-to-end
Architect and implement agentic workflows, LLM pipelines, and intelligent automation that help customers surface faster, more actionable security insights
Integrate foundation models into existing product surfaces with a practical eye toward latency, cost, output quality, and evaluation
Use AI-native development tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) as a core part of your workflow, setting the standard for how this team builds
Lead architecture and code reviews with a focus on production-grade reliability, security, and maintainability
Own projects end-to-end from concept through production, including monitoring, iteration, and improvement post-launch
Stay current with the AI tooling and foundation model landscape and bring relevant advances into our roadmap and practices

Required Qualifications:

10+ years building and shipping production software, with a track record at strong engineering companies (big tech, high-growth startups, or both)
Evidence that you drove things. We want the people who set the direction on their teams, not the ones who rode along.
Deep computer science and system design fundamentals. You can design a distributed system on a whiteboard and explain how it fails.
Heavy, hands-on use of AI coding tools on real codebases, with opinions about what works and what doesn't
Experience building with LLMs: agents, tool use, evals, prompt, and context design
Proficiency in TypeScript and strong backend engineering fundamentals
Comfort with ambiguity and a team that changes shape. You'll help define the job as we go.
Experience designing and operating distributed systems in cloud environments (AWS preferred)
Hands-on experience with CI/CD, containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and production deployment practices
Clear, direct communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

Our tech stack

TypeScript / JavaScript, Go, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL

Expect a system design round, a coding exercise where you're expected to use AI tools, and a deep dive into a project you led, including how you used AI on it. We'll ask follow-up questions until we understand the decisions you made and why.

Location and compensation:

Remote. We're hiring across United States, Canada, and Latin America.

added.description:
Our Data Scientist
roles are unique. The ideal candidate is a rare hybrid, a scientist with the programming abilities to scrape, combine, and manage data from a variety of sources and a statistician who knows how to derive insights from the information within. He or she will combine the skills to create new prototypes with the creativity and thoroughness to ask and answer the deepest questions about the data, what secrets it holds, and to push the boundaries of what is possible with big data. Want to know more?

Job Description

As a Data Scientist (P3) on the Fraud Modeling Team, you will lead the design, development, and deployment of high-impact machine learning and advanced statistical models to combat First-Party Fraud, Third-Party Fraud, Synthetic Identity Fraud, and support Identity Graph Analytics.

Operating independently within a collaborative matrixed environment, you will bridge technical model execution with commercial outcomes. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional partners—including Product, Sales, Core Analytics, and Model Risk Management (MRM)—to build stress-tested, deployable fraud detection engines, ensure regulatory alignment, and communicate technical business impact to leadership.

What You'll Do

Fraud Model Development & Optimization: Independently design, train, and optimize predictive models using XGBoost, Gradient Boosted Trees, Transformer-based models, and deep learning architectures tailored for high-dimensional, imbalanced fraud datasets.
Identity Graph & Identity Analytics: Leverage graph structures and identity link analysis to detect synthetic identity networks, fraud rings, and suspicious identity resolution patterns across large datasets.
Domain Focus Areas: Develop actionable fraud detection frameworks targeting First-Party Fraud, Third-Party Fraud, and Synthetic Identity Fraud.
Stakeholder Management & Governance:

to provide hands-on technical leadership across complex healthcare data and technology initiatives. Lead technical architecture and development:
Design, build, and deploy sophisticated data integration solutions using Palantir Foundry, including multi-source data pipelines, incremental processing, and complex data transformations.

Drive advanced engineering initiatives:
Develop and optimize solutions using Python, SQL, Java, TypeScript, and distributed computing technologies such as PySpark, while leveraging lightweight processing frameworks where appropriate.

Own technical engagements from initial discovery and solution design through development, testing, deployment, and ongoing operationalization. Partner directly with senior stakeholders to translate business needs into effective technical solutions.

Extensive hands-on experience with Palantir Foundry
, including data integration, pipeline development, Ontology architecture, application development, and enterprise deployments.

, along with experience using PySpark and modern data processing frameworks such as Pandas, Polars, or DuckDB.

added.description:
Introduction

At IBM Global Sales, we bring together innovation, collaboration, and expertise to help clients solve their most complex business challenges. Working across industries and geographies, you'll partner with colleagues, clients, and partners to co-create solutions that drive digital transformation and lasting impact.Success in Global Sales is built on curiosity, empathy, and collaboration. You'll connect technical understanding with strong people skills, building trusted relationships and shaping solutions that improve business and society. With world-class onboarding, continuous learning, and a supportive culture, IBM offers the tools and opportunities to grow your career. Join us and be part of a global team that's passionate about driving innovation and making a difference.

Your Role And Responsibilities

As a Solutions Architect (SA), you will help customers leverage streaming architectures and applications to achieve their mission outcomes. In this role, you will:

Consult directly with customers to provide software architecture, design, and operations expertise that leverages your deep knowledge of and experience in Apache Kafka, the Confluent’s products, and complementary systems such as Spark, Flink, Kubernetes, and relational and NoSQL databases;
Develop and advocate best practices, gather product feedback, and help customers overcome their operational challenges;
Build a strong relationship with your customer in a very short space of time, ensuring exemplary delivery standards;
In partnership with industry leading colleagues, have the opportunity to help customers build a state-of-the-art streaming data infrastructure, and optimize and debug customers' existing deployments.

What You Will Do

Test performance and functionality of new components developed by Engineering
Write or edit documentation and knowledge base articles, including reference architecture materials and design patterns based on customer experiences. Hone your skills, building applications, or trying out new product features
