Senior Machine Learning Engineer Location:
San Francisco or remote · Full-time
About us Hum’s mission is to learn how the Earth changes by building a “world model for the entire world”: one that represents the dynamics of Earth processes, forecasts what a place looks like next, and makes that understanding useful. Founded at the University of Waterloo and backed by top investors like HF0, Climactic, Onto Ventures and angels from Firebase and OpenTable, we are a small team working on some of the largest unsolved problems.
The role As our Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you'll own the software and infrastructure that trains and serves our models, so our research scientists can stay focused on the models themselves. The rest of our engineering team is building the pipelines that ingest petabytes of earth observation and remote sensing data, and an agent that uses that data and our models to answer customer questions. You'll own everything in between, the path from ingested data into training, the systems that run experiments and large-scale training, and the inference path that delivers model outputs to the agent. You'll work closely with those engineers to fit all the pieces together, and with our AI research scientists to make the models they dream up trainable, measurable, and servable at scale, from the first small experiment through full training runs.
What you'll do Own the ML platform.
Build and run the systems for experiment tracking, distributed training at scale, and serving inference, and keep them fast, reliable, and reproducible.
Collaborate on the interfaces.
Work with our engineers and scientists to define and maintain the boundaries between data and training, data and inference, and inference and the agent.
Enable multimodal training.
Build the data and model plumbing that lets us train on many sensors, observation types, and text in one model.
Go from small to large.
Help our scientists prove ideas in fast, cheap experiments, then scale the winners to petabyte-scale training runs.
Make evaluation real.
Implement and improve our benchmarks and evaluation frameworks, both internal and user-facing.
Watch the meter.
Measure and optimize the cost and wall-clock time of experiments, training, and inference.
Support the agent.
Work with the product team on how the agent calls the model and consumes its outputs, and build the integration.

Requirements Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years of relevant industry experience, including hands-on machine learning engineering.
Proficiency building distributed, multi-node training pipelines in PyTorch and Lightning.
Experience with AWS or another cloud platform, particularly the tooling for training and serving medium-to-large models.
Strong software engineering fundamentals: you write production-quality Python and care about reliability, observability, and cost.
Fluent with modern agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and current on how to use them well.

Bonus Experience training large diffusion or transformer models, ideally on video or time-series data.
Experience with multimodal or spatiotemporal data, geospatial data, or geoscience problems.
Experience serving models in production and integrating them with downstream applications or agents.
Startup experience, comfortable with a small, fast-moving team.

Why us? Work that matters for the planet.
Our customers in nature conservation, carbon removal, and government use our models to protect ecosystems and respond to a changing climate. We take positive impact seriously, including safety and guardrails, and you'll help us get it right.
A team worth joining.
Founded at the University of Waterloo by PhDs and engineers who've built and shipped at scale, we're small, technical, and collaborative. You'll work alongside people who care about the problem as much as you do.
Well backed.
$10M+ raised from HF0, Inovia Capital, and Propeller Ventures, angels including the cofounders of Firebase and OpenTable, and partners like AWS and the United Nations.
Compensation and upside.
Competitive salary, meaningful early-stage equity, health, dental and vision. As one of the first AI hires, your equity stake reflects that.

Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the School of Engineering Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring freeze.

For Stanford University employees, please apply through the Opportunity Marketplace within Sequoia.

Note: This is a 3-year fixed term position.

Work Arrangement

This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement with a minimum of 3 days/week working at the Stanford main campus, subject to operational needs.

Budgeted Salary

The budgeted base salary range for this position is $125,000 to $225,000 per annum.

The School of Engineering

Stanford Engineering has been at the forefront of innovation for over a century, creating pivotal technologies that have transformed the worlds of information technology, communications, health care, energy, business and beyond. Our faculty and students are creative risk-takers who pursue excellence across a breadth of disciplines. Our alumni include some of the world's most successful leaders in technology and business. Our staff are critical to enabling Stanford Engineering to accomplish its mission: seeking solutions to some of the world's most urgent challenges and educating leaders who will make the world a better place through the power of engineering principles, techniques and systems.

Founded in 1965, the Stanford Computer Science (CS) Department continues to lead the world in computer science research and education. Throughout the past five decades, the Stanford CS Department has influenced society at levels that remain without parallel among academic institutions. Its spin-offs are among the most successful corporate ventures in the world, and many of the leaders in academic and corporate research world are graduates of the Stanford CS Department.

Prof. Jure Leskovec is inviting applications for a Research Engineer
position in the Stanford Machine Learning group. Our research develops next-generation AI systems for scientific discovery and complex structured data. We build foundation models and AI agents that can learn, reason, and generalize across large-scale relational, multimodal, and multi-scale systems—from databases and knowledge graphs to molecules, cells, patients, and populations. Current research directions include foundation models for biology and the AI virtual cell, autonomous AI scientists and agents, relational and graph foundation models, multimodal and multi-scale learning, and new architectures for reasoning over structured data. A major focus is AI for biomedicine, including understanding biological systems, precision medicine, and accelerating drug discovery.

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Engineer with a strong background in machine learning and computer science to join our group and contribute to ambitious, high-impact research.

Core Duties

Play an active role in the execution and coordination of the group’s research activities, helping advance projects from initial ideas through experimentation, publication, and dissemination.
Responsibilities will include contributing to research and publications as well as preparing grant proposals, progress reports, and final reports.
You may also help mentor postdoctoral scholars, graduate students, and undergraduate researchers, and contribute to the development and teaching of graduate-level courses in machine learning and related areas.
The position is intended for someone who can combine strong technical research skills with the ability to help lead and organize a broad academic research program.

Qualifications

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

PhD in Machine Learning or Computer Science or equivalent experience.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Excellent problem solving, written and oral communication skills.
Strong organizational skills.
Ability to lead and manage projects with a high degree of independence.

Desired Qualifications

Familiarity with government funding agencies and academic research funding process.
Experience with teaching graduate level courses.
Research experience related to AI & machine learning.
Prior experience in technical writing.
Capacity to communicate information in a manner easily understood.
